# Overview



**Lobster AI** is an open-source, multi-agent bioinformatics analysis system that orchestrates 22+ specialist agents across 10 installable domain packages — all coordinated by a LangGraph supervisor and executed locally on your machine. You describe your analysis in plain language; the supervisor classifies, routes, and delegates to the right specialist, which calls validated scientific libraries directly rather than generating scripts. Every step is tracked with W3C-PROV provenance and exportable as a reproducible Jupyter notebook.

![Lobster AI Banner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-omics-os/lobster/main/docs/assets/banner.png)

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L1-L50), [lobster/agents/supervisor.py](/lobster/agents/supervisor.py#L57-L95)

## What Lobster Does

Lobster solves a core bottleneck in computational biology: turning a natural-language research request — *"Download this GEO dataset, run QC, integrate batches with Harmony, cluster, and annotate cell types"* — into a fully executed, provenance-tracked analysis pipeline. The system is built on three architectural commitments. **First**, all computation runs locally; patient data and proprietary datasets never leave your hardware. **Second**, agents invoke scientific libraries (Scanpy, PyDESeq2, Harmony, PLINK) through typed tool functions — not by generating ad-hoc code that might hallucinate parameters. **Third**, every data-loading, transformation, and export step is recorded in a W3C-PROV-style provenance log, enabling one-click export to a self-contained Jupyter notebook that any collaborator can re-run.

| Capability | How It Works |
|---|---|
| **Natural-language analysis** | Supervisor agent classifies your request, then delegates to specialist agents via typed handoff tools |
| **Local-first execution** | All analysis runs on your machine; no patient data leaves your hardware |
| **Validated scientific libraries** | Agents call Scanpy, PyDESeq2, Harmony, PLINK, etc. through tool functions — no generated scripts |
| **W3C-PROV provenance** | Every step is tracked in a `provenance.jsonl` log with activity, entity, and agent records |
| **Notebook export** | One-click export of any session as a reproducible Jupyter notebook via `/pipeline export` |
| **Plugin extensibility** | New agents register via Python entry points; `lobster scaffold` generates a contract-compliant package |

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L122-L160), [lobster/core/provenance/provenance.py](/lobster/core/provenance/provenance.py#L1-L45)

## Architecture at a Glance

The system follows a **supervisor-worker topology**: a single LangGraph supervisor classifies every user message and delegates to specialist agents implemented as ReAct sub-graphs. The supervisor communicates with workers exclusively through typed handoff tools (`handoff_to_<agent_name>`), and workers return results back to the supervisor, which synthesizes a response for the user. This means you, the user, only ever interact with the supervisor — the specialist agents are invisible implementation details.

> [!TIP]
> The Tool Calling pattern is the key architectural decision: every agent delegation is a LangGraph tool invocation, not a message-passing hop. This gives the supervisor native control over parallel vs. sequential execution and enables token-level streaming of agent transitions.

```mermaid
graph TD
    User["👤 User"] -->|Natural language| Supervisor["🧠 Supervisor Agent"]
    Supervisor -->|handoff_to_*| T1["Transcriptomics Expert"]
    Supervisor -->|handoff_to_*| R1["Research Agent"]
    Supervisor -->|handoff_to_*| G1["Genomics Expert"]
    Supervisor -->|handoff_to_*| P1["Proteomics Expert"]
    Supervisor -->|handoff_to_*| DD["Drug Discovery Expert"]
    Supervisor -->|handoff_to_*| ML["ML Expert"]
    Supervisor -->|handoff_to_*| V1["Visualization Expert"]
    T1 -->|Child delegation| AE["Annotation Expert"]
    T1 -->|Child delegation| DE["DE Analysis Expert"]
    R1 -->|Child delegation| DA["Data Expert Agent"]

    subgraph Core Services
        DM["DataManagerV2<br/>Multi-omics data orchestration"]
        PT["ProvenanceTracker<br/>W3C-PROV audit trail"]
        CR["ComponentRegistry<br/>Entry point discovery"]
    end

    T1 --- DM
    R1 --- DM
    G1 --- DM
    P1 --- DM
    DD --- DM
    ML --- DM
    DM --- PT
    CR -.->|Discovers agents| Supervisor
```

Sources: [lobster/agents/graph.py](/lobster/agents/graph.py#L1-L55), [lobster/agents/supervisor.py](/lobster/agents/supervisor.py#L57-L165), [lobster/core/runtime/data_manager.py](/lobster/core/runtime/data_manager.py#L1-L45)

## The Agent Ecosystem

Lobster ships 22 specialist agents distributed across 12 installable packages. The core `lobster-ai` package provides the supervisor, graph topology, data manager, and shared infrastructure. Domain agents live in separate packages that you install on demand — this keeps the base installation lean and lets you compose exactly the capabilities you need.

| Package | Agents | Domain |
|---|---|---|
| `lobster-transcriptomics` | transcriptomics_expert, annotation_expert, de_analysis_expert | Single-cell & bulk RNA-seq |
| `lobster-research` | research_agent, data_expert_agent | Literature discovery & data management |
| `lobster-proteomics` | proteomics_expert, proteomics_de_analysis_expert, biomarker_discovery_expert | Mass spectrometry & affinity proteomics |
| `lobster-genomics` | genomics_expert, variant_analysis_expert | GWAS, variant annotation, VCF/PLINK |
| `lobster-drug-discovery` | drug_discovery_expert, cheminformatics_expert, clinical_dev_expert, pharmacogenomics_expert | Drug discovery & cheminformatics |
| `lobster-ml` | machine_learning_expert, feature_selection_expert, survival_analysis_expert | ML data preparation & export |
| `lobster-metabolomics` | metabolomics_expert | Metabolomics data analysis |
| `lobster-visualization` | visualization_expert_agent | Single-cell & general visualizations |
| `lobster-metadata` | metadata_assistant | Sample ID mapping & schema standardization |
| `lobster-structural-viz` | protein_structure_visualization_expert | PDB fetching & ChimeraX visualization |

Agents follow a **parent-child hierarchy**: the transcriptomics expert, for example, can delegate to its child annotation expert and DE analysis expert without routing back through the supervisor. Child agents are not directly accessible to the supervisor — they are reached through their parent, which maintains domain coherence.

> [!TIP]
> Only install the packages you need. `pip install lobster-ai lobster-transcriptomics` gives you the supervisor plus transcriptomics agents. Add `lobster-genomics` later when you need GWAS support — the ComponentRegistry discovers newly installed agents automatically on next launch.

Sources: [packages/README.md](/packages/README.md#L1-L113), [lobster/core/component_registry.py](/lobster/core/component_registry.py#L69-L119)

## How Agents Are Discovered

Lobster uses **Python entry points** for zero-coupling plugin discovery. When you install `lobster-transcriptomics`, that package registers its agents in its `pyproject.toml` under the `lobster.agents` entry point group. At runtime, the `ComponentRegistry` scans all installed entry points across six groups — agents, services, adapters, providers, download services, and queue preparers — and builds the available agent roster. This means adding a new agent never requires modifying core code; it only requires publishing a package with the right entry points.

```
pyproject.toml (in lobster-transcriptomics)
  [project.entry-points."lobster.agents"]
  transcriptomics_expert = "lobster.agents.transcriptomics.transcriptomics_expert:AGENT_CONFIG"
  annotation_expert     = "lobster.agents.transcriptomics.annotation_expert:AGENT_CONFIG"
```

Each agent module exposes an `AGENT_CONFIG` dataclass at the top of its file — before any heavy imports — enabling sub-50-millisecond discovery without loading the agent's full dependency tree.

Sources: [packages/README.md](/packages/README.md#L61-L95), [lobster/core/component_registry.py](/lobster/core/component_registry.py#L69-L119), [lobster/config/agent_registry.py](/lobster/config/agent_registry.py#L25-L72)

## Core Infrastructure Layers

Behind the agents, three infrastructure layers make the system work reliably across omics domains.

| Layer | Module | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **Data Orchestration** | `lobster.core.runtime.data_manager` | Manages multi-modal datasets (AnnData, MuData), storage backends (H5AD, MuData), modality adapters, and validation |
| **Provenance Tracking** | `lobster.core.provenance.provenance` | W3C-PROV-style audit trail: activities, entities, and agents logged to `provenance.jsonl` with disk persistence |
| **Component Registry** | `lobster.core.component_registry` | Single source of truth for discovering agents, services, adapters, providers, and queue preparers via entry points |

The **DataManagerV2** is the central data orchestrator. It loads datasets into modality-specific adapters (transcriptomics, proteomics, genomics, metabolomics), stores them in typed backends (H5AD for AnnData, MuData for multi-modal), and validates schema compliance at every step. When a specialist agent asks *"what data is loaded?"*, it queries the DataManager through the `list_available_modalities` tool.

The **ProvenanceTracker** records every data-loading, transformation, and export operation with timestamps, parameter snapshots, and software version fingerprints. This log feeds the notebook export pipeline, which reconstructs a linear, re-runnable Jupyter notebook from the provenance graph.

Sources: [lobster/core/runtime/data_manager.py](/lobster/core/runtime/data_manager.py#L1-L100), [lobster/core/provenance/provenance.py](/lobster/core/provenance/provenance.py#L1-L60), [lobster/core/component_registry.py](/lobster/core/component_registry.py#L1-L60)

## Project Structure

The repository is organized into distinct layers: the core engine, agent packages, external integrations, and the testing scaffold. Understanding this layout helps you navigate the codebase and know where to look when extending the system.

```
lobster/                         # Core engine
├── agents/                      # Supervisor, state definitions, graph topology
│   ├── supervisor.py            #   Supervisor prompt builder & routing logic
│   ├── state.py                 #   OverallState, TodoItem, dynamic state discovery
│   └── graph.py                 #   LangGraph graph factory & delegation tools
├── cli.py                       # Typer CLI (chat, query, init, scaffold, validate)
├── config/                      # LLM providers, agent registry, workspace config
│   ├── agent_registry.py        #   AgentRegistryConfig & facade functions
│   ├── llm_factory.py           #   Provider-agnostic LLM instantiation
│   └── providers/               #   Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Ollama, OpenAI, etc.
├── core/                        # Infrastructure: data, provenance, plugins
│   ├── component_registry.py    #   Entry point discovery for all component types
│   ├── runtime/                 #   DataManagerV2, workspace resolution
│   ├── provenance/              #   W3C-PROV tracker, analysis IR, lineage
│   └── adapters/                #   Modality adapters (transcriptomics, proteomics, etc.)
├── tools/                       # Shared tool functions (downloads, workspace, todos)
│   ├── providers/               #   External data providers (GEO, PubMed, PRIDE, etc.)
│   └── rate_limiter.py          #   Per-provider rate limiting
└── services/                    # Business logic services (analysis, metadata, peptidomics)

packages/                        # Installable agent packages (PEP 420 namespace)
├── lobster-transcriptomics/     #   Single-cell & bulk RNA-seq agents
├── lobster-genomics/            #   GWAS & variant analysis agents
├── lobster-proteomics/          #   Mass spectrometry agents
├── lobster-drug-discovery/      #   Drug discovery & cheminformatics agents
├── lobster-ml/                  #   Machine learning agents
├── lobster-research/            #   Literature & data discovery agents
├── lobster-metabolomics/        #   Metabolomics agent
├── lobster-visualization/       #   Visualization agent
├── lobster-metadata/            #   Sample ID mapping agent
├── lobster-structural-viz/      #   Protein structure visualization agent
├── lobster-vector/              #   Vector/embedding agent
└── lobster-ai-tui/              #   Terminal UI (Go)

lobster-tui/                     # Go-based TUI frontend
tests/                           # Comprehensive test suites (unit, integration, chaos, security)
```

Sources: [packages/README.md](/packages/README.md#L42-L60), [lobster/__main__.py](/lobster/__main__.py#L1-L13), [lobster/core/runtime/workspace.py](/lobster/core/runtime/workspace.py#L1-L45)

## The Request Lifecycle

When you type a message in `lobster chat`, a precise sequence of events unfolds. Understanding this lifecycle demystifies what happens between your keystroke and the agent's response.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant CLI as CLI (Typer)
    participant S as Supervisor
    participant A as Specialist Agent
    participant DM as DataManagerV2
    participant PT as ProvenanceTracker

    U->>CLI: "Cluster this dataset with Harmony"
    CLI->>S: Message routed to LangGraph supervisor
    S->>S: Classify request (B: single-agent task)
    S->>DM: list_available_modalities (data inspection)
    DM-->>S: Loaded modalities & dimensions
    S->>A: handoff_to_transcriptomics_expert(task)
    A->>DM: Load / transform AnnData
    A->>PT: Record analysis step
    PT-->>A: Step logged to provenance.jsonl
    A-->>S: Clustering results + metadata
    S-->>CLI: Synthesized response
    CLI-->>U: Formatted output with plots
```

The supervisor first **classifies** every incoming request into one of four categories: (A) direct answer, (B) single-agent task, (C) multi-step pipeline, or (D) custom code fallback. For multi-step pipelines, it creates a todo plan via `write_todos` before delegating, then executes steps sequentially. At every handoff, the supervisor passes concise, machine-readable context — not the full conversation — keeping token costs bounded.

Sources: [lobster/agents/supervisor.py](/lobster/agents/supervisor.py#L107-L165), [lobster/agents/graph.py](/lobster/agents/graph.py#L200-L280)

# Quick Start



Get Lobster AI running on your machine in under five minutes. This guide walks you through installation, LLM provider configuration, and your first interactive analysis session — everything you need to go from zero to a working multi-agent bioinformatics system.

![Lobster AI Banner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-omics-os/lobster/main/docs/assets/banner.png)

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L1-L7), [lobster/version.py](lobster/version.py#L1-L2)

## Prerequisites

Lobster AI requires **Python 3.12 or 3.13** (3.14+ is not yet supported). The package enforces this at startup with a clear version guard — if you attempt to run on an older Python, you'll see an immediate error with remediation instructions. You also need an LLM provider API key (Anthropic, Gemini, OpenAI, or a local Ollama installation) to power the agent orchestration layer.

| Requirement | Minimum | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Python** | 3.12 (≤ 3.13) | Enforced at CLI startup |
| **LLM Provider** | 1 active | Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure, Ollama, OpenRouter, or Omics-OS Cloud |
| **OS** | macOS / Linux / Windows | Windows uses PowerShell installer |
| **Disk** | ~500 MB base | Domain packages add 200–800 MB each |

Sources: [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L9-L14), [lobster/cli.py](lobster/cli.py#L25-L34), [lobster/config/constants.py](lobster/config/constants.py#L15-L24)

## Step 1 — Install Lobster AI

The fastest path is the one-liner installer, which handles Python version detection, virtual environment creation, and the `lobster` CLI registration automatically.

**macOS / Linux:**
```bash
curl -fsSL https://install.lobsterbio.com | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell):**
```powershell
irm https://install.lobsterbio.com/windows | iex
```

**Alternative — pip or uv:**
```bash
# With uv (recommended, faster)
uv tool install --python 3.13 lobster-ai

# With pip
pip install lobster-ai
```

For developers contributing to the codebase, the Makefile provides a full development installation with all domain packages and test dependencies:
```bash
make dev-install
```

> [!TIP]
> The `uv tool install` method is preferred over `pip` because it creates an isolated environment that won't conflict with your system Python or other projects. The `--python 3.13` flag ensures the correct Python version is used even if your system default is older.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L23-L29), [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L9-L14), [Makefile](Makefile#L10-L24)

## Step 2 — Configure Your LLM Provider

Run the interactive initialization wizard to select and configure your LLM provider. This command writes credentials to your workspace `.env` file and installs the correct LangChain provider package.

```bash
lobster init
```

The wizard walks you through provider selection, API key entry, and agent package installation. Behind the scenes, `lobster init` uses a structured protocol to detect your environment (existing credentials, Ollama status, installed agents) and writes a deterministic configuration.

For **CI/CD or scripting**, use non-interactive mode with explicit flags:

```bash
# Anthropic Direct API
lobster init --non-interactive --anthropic-key sk-ant-...

# Local Ollama (no API key needed)
lobster init --non-interactive --use-ollama --ollama-model llama3:8b-instruct

# Google Gemini
lobster init --non-interactive --gemini-key AIza...

# OpenAI
lobster init --non-interactive --openai-key sk-...
```

The system supports **eight LLM providers**, each with a dedicated LangChain integration:

| Provider | Key Config | Display Name |
|---|---|---|
| `anthropic` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic Direct API |
| `openai` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI |
| `gemini` | `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | Google Gemini |
| `bedrock` | `AWS_BEDROCK_ACCESS_KEY` + `AWS_BEDROCK_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | AWS Bedrock |
| `azure` | `AZURE_AI_ENDPOINT` + `AZURE_AI_CREDENTIAL` | Azure AI |
| `ollama` | No key required (local) | Ollama (Local) |
| `openrouter` | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | OpenRouter (600+ models) |
| `omics-os` | Cloud credentials via `lobster auth login` | Omics-OS Cloud |

You can also specify an **agent profile** that controls model selection and behavior:

```bash
lobster init --profile production   # Balanced cost/quality
lobster init --profile performance  # Higher capability models
lobster init --profile max          # Maximum capability
```

Valid profiles are: `development`, `production`, `performance`, `max`, and `hybrid`.

> [!TIP]
> If you have Ollama installed locally, the init wizard auto-detects it and lists available models. This is the only provider that requires zero API keys — ideal for air-gapped environments or sensitive patient data that must never leave your machine.

Sources: [lobster/cli.py](lobster/cli.py#L728-L830), [lobster/config/provider_setup.py](lobster/config/provider_setup.py#L62-L157), [lobster/config/constants.py](lobster/config/constants.py#L15-L48), [lobster/cli_internal/commands/light/init_protocol.py](lobster/cli_internal/commands/light/init_protocol.py#L87-L152)

## Step 3 — Verify Connectivity

Before starting an analysis session, confirm your provider configuration is valid and the API is reachable:

```bash
lobster config-test
```

This command tests API connectivity, validates credentials, and reports any issues. You can also inspect your full configuration at any time with:

```bash
lobster config          # Show current configuration and agent composition
lobster status          # Show subscription tier, installed packages, available agents
```

Sources: [lobster/cli.py](lobster/cli.py#L547-L554), [lobster/cli.py](lobster/cli.py#L556-L558)

## Step 4 — Start Your First Session

Launch an interactive chat session where you describe your analysis in plain language:

```bash
lobster chat
```

Then describe what you need — the supervisor agent routes your request to the appropriate specialist agents automatically:

```text
> Search PubMed for single-cell CRISPR screens in T cells from 2023–2024,
  download the most cited dataset, run QC, integrate batches with Harmony,
  cluster the cells, annotate cell types, and export a reproducible notebook.
```

For **single-turn, non-interactive** usage (scripts, pipelines):

```bash
lobster query "Search PubMed for CRISPR screen datasets in T cells"
```

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L37-L54), [lobster/cli.py](lobster/cli.py#L497-L531)

## Session Workflow at a Glance

The following diagram shows the end-to-end flow from installation through your first analysis:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["<b>Install</b><br/>curl install or pip/uv"] --> B["<b>Configure</b><br/>lobster init"]
    B --> C{"Connectivity OK?"}
    C -- No --> D["<b>Fix config</b><br/>lobster config-test"]
    D --> B
    C -- Yes --> E["<b>Chat</b><br/>lobster chat"]
    E --> F["<b>Supervisor Agent</b><br/>Routes to specialist"]
    F --> G["<b>Specialist Agents</b><br/>Execute validated tools"]
    G --> H["<b>Results</b><br/>Data + plots + provenance"]
    H --> I["<b>Export</b><br/>/pipeline export → notebook"]
    I --> E
```

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L23-L70), [lobster/cli.py](lobster/cli.py#L547-L558)

## In-Session Slash Commands

Once inside `lobster chat`, use slash commands to manage your session:

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/pipeline export` | Export analysis as a reproducible Jupyter notebook |
| `/pipeline run analysis.ipynb` | Re-run an exported notebook |
| `/data` | List loaded datasets and modalities |
| `/files` | Browse workspace files |
| `/status` | Session info, token usage, active agents |
| `/help` | Show all slash commands |

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L56-L70)

## Session Continuity

Lobster supports **session persistence** — you can resume conversations across multiple CLI invocations using `--session-id`:

```bash
# Start a named session
lobster query --session-id my_project "Search PubMed for CRISPR screens"

# Resume it later
lobster query --session-id latest "Download the first result"

# Or continue in interactive mode
lobster chat --session-id my_project
```

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L72-L76)

## Install Domain Packages

The base `lobster-ai` package includes the core agent framework and CLI. Domain-specific capabilities are installed as optional extras, each bundling the relevant agent, its scientific dependencies, and visualization tools:

```bash
# Single-cell and bulk RNA-seq
pip install lobster-ai[transcriptomics]

# VCF, GWAS, variant annotation
pip install lobster-ai[genomics]

# DDA/DIA mass spectrometry
pip install lobster-ai[proteomics]

# Literature search and dataset discovery
pip install lobster-ai[research]

# Everything at once
pip install lobster-ai[full]
```

| Extra | Agents Included | Key Capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| `[transcriptomics]` | scRNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq | QC, batch integration (Harmony/scVI), clustering, cell annotation, trajectory inference |
| `[genomics]` | Genomics expert | GWAS, LD pruning, variant annotation, association testing |
| `[proteomics]` | Proteomics expert | DDA/DIA processing, biomarker panel selection, network analysis |
| `[research]` | Research agent | PubMed search, dataset discovery, automated literature mining |
| `[full]` | All of the above | Complete multi-omics suite |

Sources: [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L137-L193), [README.md](README.md#L147-L175)

## Build Your Own Agent (Optional)

If you want to extend Lobster with a custom domain agent, the `scaffold` command generates a complete, contract-compliant plugin package:

```bash
lobster scaffold agent \
  --name epigenomics_expert \
  --display-name "Epigenomics Expert" \
  --description "ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, and DNA methylation analysis"
```

This creates a directory structure with `pyproject.toml`, entry point wiring, tool stubs with AQUADIF metadata, and contract tests. Validate your package before distribution:

```bash
lobster validate-plugin ./lobster-epigenomics/
```

Sources: [lobster/cli_internal/commands/light/scaffold_commands.py](lobster/cli_internal/commands/light/scaffold_commands.py#L26-L76), [README.md](README.md#L97-L116)

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Error: Python 3.12+ required` | Old Python version | `uv tool install --python 3.13 lobster-ai` |
| `lobster: command not found` | CLI not on PATH | Re-run installer, or use `uv tool install` |
| Init wizard doesn't detect Ollama | Ollama not running | `ollama serve` in a separate terminal |
| API key rejected | Invalid or expired key | Run `lobster init` again, or check `lobster config-test` |
| Agent not found at runtime | Domain package missing | `pip install lobster-ai[transcriptomics]` (or relevant extra) |
| SSL certificate errors | Corporate proxy/firewall | `lobster init --no-ssl-verify` or `--ssl-cert-path /path/to/ca.pem` |

Sources: [lobster/cli.py](lobster/cli.py#L25-L34), [lobster/cli.py](lobster/cli.py#L830-L855), [lobster/config/provider_setup.py](lobster/config/provider_setup.py#L34-L60)

# CLI Reference



The Lobster CLI is your primary interface to the multi-agent bioinformatics system. Built on **Typer** with **Rich** terminal rendering, it provides commands for configuration, interactive analysis, agent management, cloud connectivity, and plugin development — all accessible from a single `lobster` entry point. The CLI requires **Python 3.12+** and validates this at startup before any heavy imports occur.

Sources: [cli.py](/lobster/cli.py#L1-L27), [__main__.py](/lobster/__main__.py#L1-L13)

## Command Architecture

The CLI is organized into a **two-tier command hierarchy**: top-level commands for everyday workflows (`init`, `chat`, `query`) and subcommand groups for domain-specific management (`agents`, `auth`, `cloud`, `scaffold`, `validate-plugin`). Behind the scenes, the implementation is split into **light commands** (fast, minimal imports from `cli_internal/commands/light/`) and **heavy commands** (lazily loaded from `cli_internal/commands/heavy/` to preserve startup speed). This lazy-loading strategy saves approximately 5 seconds of import time at launch.

Sources: [cli.py](/lobster/cli.py#L70-L74), [cli.py](/lobster/cli.py#L79-L88)

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["lobster"] --> B["Top-Level Commands"]
    A --> C["Subcommand Groups"]
    
    B --> B1["init"]
    B --> B2["chat"]
    B --> B3["query"]
    B --> B4["config / config-test"]
    B --> B5["status"]
    B --> B6["metadata"]
    B --> B7["activate / deactivate"]
    B --> B8["purge"]
    B --> B9["dashboard"]
    
    C --> C1["agents<br/>list · info · install · uninstall"]
    C --> C2["auth<br/>login · logout · status"]
    C --> C3["cloud<br/>login · status · logout · chat"]
    C --> C4["scaffold<br/>agent"]
    C --> C5["validate-plugin"]
    
    style A fill:#E85D2C,color:#fff
    style B fill:#2D6A4F,color:#fff
    style C fill:#2D6A4F,color:#fff
```

## Global Flags

These flags are available on the root `lobster` command before any subcommand:

| Flag | Short | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `--version` | `-v` | Print the current Lobster version and exit |
| `--help` | | Show the help guide with all available commands |

Running `lobster` with no arguments displays a friendly help guide and checks for updates (non-blocking, cached, fails silently if offline).

Sources: [cli.py](/lobster/cli.py#L369-L397), [cli.py](/lobster/cli.py#L139)

## `lobster init`

Initialize Lobster AI configuration. This is the **first command you run** after installation — it sets up provider credentials, model selection, and agent composition for your workspace.

**Usage:**
```bash
lobster init [OPTIONS]
```

**Key Options:**

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--global`, `-g` | Save configuration to `~/.config/lobster/` (applies to all workspaces) |
| `--force`, `-f` | Overwrite existing configuration |
| `--non-interactive` | CI/CD mode — requires API key flags, no prompts |
| `--anthropic-key` | Claude API key (non-interactive) |
| `--bedrock-access-key` | AWS Bedrock access key (non-interactive) |
| `--bedrock-secret-key` | AWS Bedrock secret key (non-interactive) |
| `--use-ollama` | Use Ollama local LLM provider |
| `--ollama-model` | Ollama model name (default: `llama3:8b-instruct`) |
| `--model`, `-m` | Default model ID for the selected provider |
| `--gemini-key` | Google API key (non-interactive) |
| `--openai-key` | OpenAI API key (non-interactive) |
| `--openrouter-key` | OpenRouter API key (non-interactive) |
| `--azure-endpoint` | Azure AI endpoint URL (non-interactive) |
| `--azure-credential` | Azure AI API credential (non-interactive) |
| `--profile` | Agent profile: `development`, `production`, `performance`, `max` |
| `--agents` | Comma-separated list of agents to enable |
| `--preset` | Agent preset: `scrna-basic`, `scrna-full`, `multiomics-full` |
| `--auto-agents` | Use LLM to suggest agents based on a description |
| `--agents-description` | Workflow description for LLM agent suggestion |
| `--cloud-key` | Lobster Cloud API key (enables premium tier) |
| `--ui` | UI mode for interactive init: `auto`, `go`, `classic` |
| `--skip-extras` | Skip optional package installation |

> [!TIP]
> Credential resolution follows a strict priority chain: **workspace `.env`** (highest) → **global `credentials.env`** (`~/.config/lobster/`) → **environment variables** (lowest). This means a workspace `.env` always overrides global settings, enabling project-specific provider configurations.

**Common Examples:**
```bash
# Interactive setup (workspace-local)
lobster init

# Interactive setup (global defaults for all workspaces)
lobster init --global

# CI/CD: Claude API with production profile
lobster init --non-interactive --anthropic-key=sk-ant-xxx --profile=production

# CI/CD: Ollama with a custom model
lobster init --non-interactive --use-ollama --ollama-model=mixtral:8x7b-instruct

# CI/CD: OpenRouter (600+ models available)
lobster init --non-interactive --openrouter-key=sk-or-xxx

# CI/CD: Azure AI
lobster init --non-interactive --azure-endpoint=https://xxx.inference.ai.azure.com/ --azure-credential=xxx

# Force reconfiguration
lobster init --force
```

Sources: [cli.py](/lobster/cli.py#L797-L1022)

## `lobster chat`

Start an **interactive chat session** with the multi-agent system. This is the primary command for exploratory bioinformatics analysis — you converse with specialized agents that route your questions to the right domain expert.

**Usage:**
```bash
lobster chat [OPTIONS]
```

**Key Options:**

| Option | Short | Description |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| `--workspace` | `-w` | Workspace directory (default: `./.lobster_workspace` or `LOBSTER_WORKSPACE` env var) |
| `--session-id` | `-s` | Continue a saved session; use `latest` for most recent |
| `--reasoning` | | Show agent reasoning and thinking process |
| `--verbose` | `-v` | Show detailed tool usage and agent activity |
| `--debug` | `-d` | Enable debug mode with enhanced error reporting |
| `--profile-timings` | | Enable timing diagnostics for data manager operations |
| `--provider` | `-p` | Override LLM provider (`bedrock`, `anthropic`, `ollama`) |
| `--model` | `-m` | Override model (e.g., `claude-4-sonnet`, `llama3:70b-instruct`) |
| `--stream` / `--no-stream` | | Enable/disable real-time text streaming (default: on) |
| `--no-intro` | | Disable Go TUI intro animation (useful for automation) |
| `--ui` | | UI mode: `auto` (Go TUI → classic fallback), `go` (require Go TUI), `classic` (Rich terminal) |
| `--classic` | | Shorthand for `--ui classic` |

The chat command first attempts to launch the **Go TUI** (a high-performance terminal UI written in Go). If the Go binary isn't installed or the terminal isn't interactive, it falls back to the **classic Rich terminal** interface. The `--classic` flag short-circuits this detection and forces the Python-based UI.

> [!TIP]
> Use `--session-id latest` to resume your most recent conversation. Session data is stored under `.lobster/sessions/` in your workspace, preserving full conversation context and agent routing history across restarts.

**Common Examples:**
```bash
# Start a new interactive session
lobster chat

# Continue most recent session
lobster chat --session-id latest

# Use a specific session
lobster chat --session-id session_20241208_150000

# Show agent reasoning (great for learning how agents work)
lobster chat --reasoning

# Force classic terminal UI
lobster chat --classic

# Override provider and model
lobster chat --provider anthropic --model claude-4-sonnet
```

Sources: [cli.py](/lobster/cli.py#L1225-L1337)

## `lobster query`

Run a **single query** against the multi-agent system without entering an interactive session. Ideal for scripted workflows, quick lookups, or pipeline integration.

**Usage:**
```bash
lobster query "Your question here" [OPTIONS]
```

**Key Options:**

| Option | Short | Description |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| `--workspace` | `-w` | Workspace directory |
| `--session-id` | `-s` | Continue a saved session |
| `--reasoning` | | Show agent reasoning |
| `--verbose` | `-v` | Show agent and tool trace details |
| `--debug` | `-d` | Enable debug logging |
| `--output` | `-o` | Write the final answer to a file |
| `--profile-timings` | | Enable timing diagnostics |
| `--provider` | `-p` | Override LLM provider |
| `--model` | `-m` | Override model |

**Common Examples:**
```bash
# Single query
lobster query "What pathways are enriched in my DEG list?"

# Save output to file
lobster query "Summarize the sample metadata" --output results.txt

# Query with a specific provider
lobster query "Cluster these cells" --provider anthropic --model claude-4-sonnet
```

Sources: [cli.py](/lobster/cli.py#L1367-L1394)

## `lobster dashboard`

Launch the **Textual TUI dashboard** — a rich, interactive terminal application for visualizing workspace data, session history, and agent activity.

**Usage:**
```bash
lobster dashboard [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Short | Description |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| `--workspace` | `-w` | Workspace directory |

This command requires the `textual` package. If not installed, the CLI will print the install command.

Sources: [cli.py](/lobster/cli.py#L1340-L1364)

## `lobster config`

Display and manage your current configuration including agent composition, provider settings, and workspace details.

**Usage:**
```bash
lobster config [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Short | Description |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| `--workspace` | `-w` | Workspace directory to inspect |

Running `lobster config` without a subcommand shows a configuration summary. Subcommands (like `lobster config show`, `lobster config list-models`) provide more detailed views.

Sources: [cli.py](/lobster/cli.py#L303-L346)

## `lobster config-test`

Test **API connectivity** and validate that your configuration is working correctly. Reports which providers are reachable and whether credentials are valid.

**Usage:**
```bash

```

| Option | Short | Description |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| `--json` | `-j` | Output results as JSON (machine-readable) |

Display your **subscription tier**, installed packages, and available agents in a summary view.

**Usage:**
```bash
lobster status
```

## `lobster metadata`

Display metadata overview and statistics about your workspace data, publications, samples, and exports.

**Usage:**
```bash
lobster metadata [SUBCOMMAND] [OPTIONS]
```

**Subcommands:**

| Subcommand | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| *(none)* | Smart overview with key stats and next steps |
| `publications` | Publication queue status breakdown |
| `samples` | Sample statistics and disease coverage |
| `workspace` | File inventory across all locations |
| `exports` | Export files with usage hints |
| `list` | Legacy detailed list |
| `clear` | Clear metadata (with `exports`/`all` options) |

**Key Options:**

| Option | Short | Description |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| `--workspace` | `-w` | Workspace directory |
| `--status` | | Status filter for `publications` subcommand |

**Common Examples:**
```bash
lobster metadata                           # Smart overview
lobster metadata publications              # Publication queue status
lobster metadata publications --status=handoff_ready
lobster metadata samples                   # Sample statistics
lobster metadata exports                   # Export files
```

Sources: [cli.py](/lobster/cli.py#L622-L663)

## `lobster activate` / `lobster deactivate`

Activate or deactivate a **premium license** using an access code from Omics-OS.

**Usage:**
```bash
lobster activate <ACCESS_CODE> [--server <URL>]
lobster deactivate
```

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--server` | Custom license server URL (default: `https://licenses.omics-os.com`) |

Deactivation removes the local license file and reverts to the free tier. Your license can be re-activated on another machine or reused later.

Sources: [cli.py](/lobster/cli.py#L666-L702)

## `lobster purge`

Remove all Lobster AI files from your system. This is a destructive operation with built-in safety guards — only directories verified to contain Lobster AI files will be removed.

**Usage:**
```bash
lobster purge [OPTIONS]
```

**Key Options:**

| Option | Short | Description |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| `--scope` | `-s` | What to purge: `global`, `workspace`, or `all` (default: `all`) |
| `--workspace` | `-w` | Workspace directory to purge |
| `--keep-license` | | Preserve license file (`~/.lobster/license.json`) |
| `--dry-run` | `-n` | Preview what would be deleted without deleting |
| `--force` | `-f` | Skip confirmation prompt |

**What gets removed:**

| Scope | Files |
|-------|-------|
| **Global** (`~/.lobster/`, `~/.config/lobster/`) | `license.json`, `providers.json`, `credentials.env`, `lobster_history`, `version_check_cache` |
| **Workspace** (`.lobster_workspace/`) | `data/`, `cache/`, `plots/`, sessions |

**Common Examples:**
```bash
lobster purge --dry-run          # Preview what would be deleted
lobster purge --scope global     # Remove only global config files
lobster purge --scope workspace  # Remove only current workspace
lobster purge --keep-license     # Preserve your license file
lobster purge --force            # Skip confirmation prompt
```

Sources: [cli.py](/lobster/cli.py#L705-L793)

## `lobster agents`

Manage agent packages — discover what's installed, inspect individual agents, and install or remove domain-specific packages.

**Usage:**
```bash
lobster agents <SUBCOMMAND>
```

**Subcommands:**

| Subcommand | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| `list` | Display all installed agents in a sorted table |
| `info <AGENT>` | Show concise card with agent details |
| `install <PACKAGE>` | Install a package via `uv pip`, auto-enable its agents |
| `uninstall <PACKAGE>` | Remove a package via `uv pip`, remove from config |

**Common Examples:**
```bash
lobster agents list                          # See all installed agents
lobster agents info research_agent           # Inspect a specific agent
lobster agents install lobster-transcriptomics  # Add transcriptomics agents
```

> [!TIP]
> In a `uv tool` environment, `agents install` is blocked because `uv pip install` writes to a venv that gets wiped on the next `uv tool upgrade`. Instead, use: `uv tool install lobster-ai --with <package>`.

Sources: [agent_commands.py](/lobster/cli_internal/commands/light/agent_commands.py#L1-L44)

## `lobster auth`

Authenticate with LLM providers that support **OAuth login**. This is separate from API key configuration (handled by `lobster init`).

**Usage:**
```bash
lobster auth <SUBCOMMAND>
```

**Subcommands:**

| Subcommand | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| `login <provider>` | Login via OAuth browser flow (currently supports `anthropic`) |
| `logout <provider>` | Remove stored OAuth credentials |
| `status` | Show authentication status for all providers |

**Login Options:**

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--no-browser` | Print the auth URL instead of opening browser |
| `--timeout` | Seconds to wait for browser callback (default: 120) |

**Common Examples:**
```bash
lobster auth login anthropic       # OAuth login with Claude account
lobster auth login anthropic --no-browser  # Headless/remote auth
lobster auth logout anthropic      # Remove stored credentials
lobster auth status                # Check all provider statuses
```

The `status` subcommand checks authentication across all providers including Anthropic (API key + OAuth), Omics-OS Cloud, AWS Bedrock, OpenAI, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, and Azure AI — reporting the method and state for each.

Sources: [auth_commands.py](/lobster/cli_internal/commands/light/auth_commands.py#L1-L31), [auth_commands.py](/lobster/cli_internal/commands/light/auth_commands.py#L90-L162)

## `lobster cloud`

Manage your **Omics-OS Cloud** connection — authenticate, check usage and budget, and launch cloud-based chat sessions.

**Usage:**
```bash
lobster cloud <SUBCOMMAND>
```

**Subcommands:**

| Subcommand | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| `login` | Authenticate with Omics-OS Cloud (API key or browser OAuth) |
| `status` | Show current usage and remaining budget |
| `logout` | Remove stored cloud credentials |
| `chat` | Open interactive cloud chat (launches npm TUI) |

Security is enforced at the protocol level — the CLI refuses to send credentials over non-HTTPS connections (localhost exempted for development), and the browser OAuth flow uses CSRF-protected state tokens.

Sources: [cloud_commands.py](/lobster/cli_internal/commands/light/cloud_commands.py#L1-L42)

## `lobster scaffold`

Generate **plugin packages** for extending Lobster with custom agents. The scaffold creates a complete, standards-compliant package structure ready for development.

**Usage:**
```bash
lobster scaffold agent [OPTIONS]
```

**Key Options:**

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--name` | Agent name in snake_case (e.g., `epigenomics_expert`) |
| `--display-name` | Human-readable name (e.g., "Epigenomics Expert") |
| `--description` | Agent capabilities description |
| `--children` | Comma-separated child agent names |
| `--output-dir`, `-o` | Output directory (default: `.`) |
| `--author-name` | Package author name |
| `--author-email` | Package author email |

**Common Example:**
```bash
lobster scaffold agent \
  --name epigenomics_expert \
  --display-name "Epigenomics Expert" \
  --description "Analyzes methylation and chromatin accessibility data"
```

After scaffolding, the CLI prints next steps: fill in domain-specific tools, add services and platform configs, then validate with `lobster validate-plugin`.

Sources: [scaffold_commands.py](/lobster/cli_internal/commands/light/scaffold_commands.py#L1-L76)

## `lobster validate-plugin`

Validate a plugin package for **Lobster AI contract compliance**. This runs 7 structural checks to ensure your plugin will integrate correctly with the agent system.

**Usage:**
```bash
lobster validate-plugin <PLUGIN_DIR>
```

**Checks Performed:**

| # | Check | What It Verifies |
|---|-------|-----------------|
| 1 | PEP 420 compliance | No `__init__.py` at namespace boundaries |
| 2 | Entry points | `lobster.agents` group defined in `pyproject.toml` |
| 3 | AGENT_CONFIG position | Placed before heavy imports |
| 4 | Factory signature | Standard parameters accepted |
| 5 | AQUADIF metadata | Tools have categories and provenance |
| 6 | Provenance calls | `log_tool_usage` with `ir=` parameter |
| 7 | Import boundaries | No cross-agent imports |

**Common Example:**
```bash
lobster validate-plugin ./lobster-epigenomics/
```

Sources: [validate_commands.py](/lobster/cli_internal/commands/light/validate_commands.py#L1-L59)

## Environment Variables

The CLI responds to several environment variables for workspace resolution, provider configuration, and feature flags:

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `LOBSTER_WORKSPACE` | Default workspace directory (overrides `./.lobster_workspace`) |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic/Claude API key |
| `AWS_BEDROCK_ACCESS_KEY` | AWS Bedrock access key |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI API key |
| `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | Google Gemini API key |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | OpenRouter API key |
| `AZURE_AI_CREDENTIAL` | Azure AI API credential |
| `LOBSTER_PROFILE_TIMINGS` | Enable timing diagnostics (`true`/`false`) |
| `PYDEVD_WARN_EVALUATION_TIMEOUT` | Debugger eval timeout (set to 900000 internally) |

Sources: [cli.py](/lobster/cli.py#L49), [cli.py](/lobster/cli.py#L406)

# Architecture Overview



Lobster is a **multi-agent AI orchestration platform** purpose-built for bioinformatics and multi-omics research. At its core, a LangGraph-powered supervisor agent classifies incoming requests and delegates them to domain-specialist agents — transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, genomics, drug discovery, and more. The system is designed around three architectural pillars: **hierarchical agent coordination**, **entry-point-driven extensibility**, and **provenance-tracked data management**. This page maps the full topology — from the user-facing frontends down through the agent graph, plugin registry, and data layer — so you can reason about where your contributions or customizations fit.

![Architecture Topology Overview](https://github.com/the-omics-os/lobster/blob/main/media/arch-topology-overview.png?raw=true)

## High-Level Topology

The system is organized as a layered architecture with strict dependency direction: frontends depend on the client layer, the client layer depends on the agent graph, and the agent graph depends on the core runtime and plugin registry. Cross-cutting concerns — configuration, security policy, provenance — span all layers but are governed from the core.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Frontends
        CLI["Python CLI<br/>(typer + rich)"]
        TUI["Go TUI<br/>(lobster-tui/)"]
    end

    subgraph Client Layer
        AC["AgentClient<br/>(local execution)"]
        CC["CloudLobsterClient<br/>(remote API)"]
        BC["BaseClient ABC"]
    end

    subgraph Agent Graph
        SUP["Supervisor Agent<br/>(LangGraph ReAct)"]
        WA1["transcriptomics_expert"]
        WA2["proteomics_expert"]
        WA3["research_agent"]
        WA4["drug_discovery_expert"]
        WAn["… more specialists"]
    end

    subgraph Core Runtime
        DM["DataManagerV2<br/>(multi-omics orchestration)"]
        CR["ComponentRegistry<br/>(entry-point discovery)"]
        PROV["Provenance Tracker<br/>(Analysis IR)"]
        QS["Queue System<br/>(download + publication)"]
    end

    subgraph Plugins & Packages
        EP["Entry Points<br/>lobster.agents<br/>lobster.services<br/>lobster.adapters<br/>lobster.providers"]
        PKG["Domain Packages<br/>lobster-transcriptomics<br/>lobster-proteomics<br/>lobster-genomics<br/>lobster-ml<br/>…"]
    end

    CLI --> AC
    TUI --> CC
    AC --> BC
    CC --> BC
    AC --> SUP
    SUP --> WA1 & WA2 & WA3 & WA4 & WAn
    WA1 & WA2 & WA3 & WA4 & WAn --> DM
    DM --> PROV & QS
    CR --> EP
    EP --> PKG
    SUP --> CR
```

Sources: [__main__.py](lobster/__main__.py#L1-L13), [cli.py](lobster/cli.py#L1-L90), [base_client.py](lobster/core/interfaces/base_client.py#L1-L182), [graph.py](lobster/agents/graph.py#L1-L50)

## Project Structure Map

The repository is a monorepo containing the core framework, a Go-based TUI, and a family of domain-specific packages. Understanding this layout is essential for navigating the codebase effectively.

```
lobster/                          # Core Python package
├── agents/                       # LangGraph graph, supervisor, state definitions
│   ├── graph.py                  # Graph assembly + agent tool creation
│   ├── supervisor.py             # Dynamic supervisor prompt builder
│   └── state.py                  # OverallState + domain-specific states
├── cli.py                        # Typer CLI entry point (1700+ lines)
├── cli_internal/                 # CLI subcommands (init, agents, scaffold, auth, cloud)
├── config/                       # LLM providers, agent registry, workspace config
│   ├── providers/                # Anthropic, Bedrock, Gemini, Ollama, OpenAI, OpenRouter
│   ├── agent_registry.py         # Agent discovery + AGENT_CONFIG resolution
│   └── supervisor_config.py      # Supervisor behavior tuning
├── core/                         # Runtime engine + data layer
│   ├── adapters/                 # Modality adapters (transcriptomics, proteomics, …)
│   ├── backends/                 # Storage backends (H5AD, MuData)
│   ├── client.py                 # AgentClient — local execution path
│   ├── component_registry.py     # Unified entry-point discovery (agents, services, adapters, providers)
│   ├── provenance/               # Analysis IR, lineage tracking
│   ├── queues/                   # Download + publication queues
│   ├── runtime/                  # DataManagerV2 + workspace resolver
│   └── interfaces/               # ABC contracts (BaseClient, IModalityAdapter, IDataBackend)
├── services/                     # Business logic services (analysis, execution, metadata, orchestration)
├── tools/                        # LangChain tool implementations (workspace, providers, rate limiting)
├── integrations/                 # External integrations
├── lobster_cloud/                # Cloud client implementation
├── prompts/                      # Prompt templates
├── scaffold/                     # Package scaffolding utilities
├── testing/                      # Test infrastructure
├── ui/                           # Terminal UI theming + console management
└── utils/                        # Shared utilities (logging, callbacks)

lobster-tui/                      # Go-based Terminal UI (cmd/, internal/, themes/)
packages/                         # Domain packages (each an installable PyPI package)
├── lobster-transcriptomics/      # scRNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq, annotation, DE analysis
├── lobster-proteomics/           # Proteomics, DE, biomarker discovery
├── lobster-genomics/             # Genomics, variant analysis
├── lobster-metabolomics/         # Metabolomics LC-MS
├── lobster-drug-discovery/       # Drug discovery, cheminformatics, clinical dev
├── lobster-ml/                   # ML, feature selection, survival analysis
├── lobster-visualization/        # Plotly-based visualization
├── lobster-structural-viz/       # Protein structure visualization
├── lobster-metadata/             # Metadata assistant
├── lobster-research/             # Research + data expert agents
├── lobster-vector/               # Vector/embedding utilities
└── lobster-visualization/        # General visualization
```

Sources: [component_registry.py](lobster/core/component_registry.py#L86-L118), [data_manager_v2.py](lobster/core/data_manager_v2.py#L1-L12), [graph.py](lobster/agents/graph.py#L1-L50)

## Agent Graph: Supervisor-Worker Topology

The heart of Lobster is its **LangGraph multi-agent graph**, assembled by `create_bioinformatics_graph()`. The architecture uses the **Tool Calling pattern** — the supervisor doesn't route via conditional edges on a `StateGraph`, but instead invokes sub-agents as LangChain tools. This means `handoff_to_<agent_name>` tools appear naturally in the supervisor's tool list, and the LLM selects which specialist to call based on the request and each tool's description.

The graph construction follows a **three-phase pipeline**:

| Phase | Function | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| **1. Resolve** | `_resolve_worker_agents()` | Discover agents from `ComponentRegistry`, apply enable-list + tier filters, auto-include child agents |
| **2. Create** | `_create_agents_single_pass()` | Import each agent's factory function, inject `DataManagerV2` + delegation tools, compile into Pregel graphs |
| **3. Assemble** | `_build_supervisor_tools()` + LangGraph assembly | Build handoff tools + workspace/code/todo tools, bind to supervisor's ReAct agent |

A critical design detail is the **lazy delegation tool** pattern. Parent agents (e.g., `transcriptomics_expert`) hold references to child agents (e.g., `annotation_expert`) via `_create_lazy_delegation_tool()`, which captures the shared `created_agents` dictionary by reference and resolves the actual agent instance at invocation time. This allows the graph to be assembled in a single pass without requiring topological ordering.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant S as Supervisor
    participant T as transcriptomics_expert
    participant A as annotation_expert
    participant DM as DataManagerV2

    U->>S: "Analyze my scRNA-seq data and annotate cell types"
    Note over S: Classifies as (C) MULTI-STEP PIPELINE
    S->>S: write_todos(["Download data", "QC + clustering", "Annotation"])
    S->>T: handoff_to_transcriptomics_expert("Perform QC and Leiden clustering")
    T->>DM: Load + process AnnData
    T-->>S: Clustering results + store_key
    S->>T: handoff_to_transcriptomics_expert("Delegate annotation to annotation_expert")
    T->>A: handoff_to_annotation_expert("Annotate clusters from Leiden results")
    A->>DM: Read modality metadata
    A-->>T: Cell type annotations
    T-->>S: Full results with annotations
    S-->>U: Summarized analysis + plots
```

Sources: [graph.py](lobster/agents/graph.py#L227-L301), [graph.py](lobster/agents/graph.py#L304-L391), [graph.py](lobster/agents/graph.py#L678-L794), [supervisor.py](lobster/agents/supervisor.py#L131-L157)

## State Management and Graph Topology

All agents share a common state schema rooted in `OverallState`, which extends LangGraph's `AgentState`. The supervisor operates directly on `OverallState`, while specialist agents extend it with domain-specific fields (e.g., `clustering_results` for transcriptomics). State flows through the graph via LangGraph's standard message-passing — the `messages` field accumulates the conversation, while custom fields like `todos`, `store_keys`, and `context_compaction` support planning, context management, and trimming visibility.

The `todos` field uses a **replace reducer** (`_todo_reducer`) rather than append, because the supervisor sends the complete current plan on each `write_todos` call — matching the DeepAgents/LangChain TodoListMiddleware pattern. The `store_keys` registry maps store keys to agent names, populated by a `pre_model_hook` so that key references survive message trimming.

> [!TIP]
> Domain packages extend `OverallState` via the `lobster.states` entry point group. The `get_all_state_classes()` function discovers these at runtime, so new state schemas from installed packages are automatically available without modifying core code.

Sources: [state.py](lobster/agents/state.py#L1-L186), [state.py](lobster/agents/state.py#L27-L83)

## Plugin System and Entry Points

Lobster's extensibility model is built entirely on **Python entry points** — the standard mechanism for packages to advertise components to a host application. The `ComponentRegistry` is the single source of truth, scanning six entry-point groups at load time:

| Entry Point Group | Purpose | Contract |
|-------------------|---------|----------|
| `lobster.agents` | Agent configurations | `AGENT_CONFIG` dataclass with factory_function, description, routing_keywords |
| `lobster.services` | Service classes | Instantiable class or factory callable |
| `lobster.adapters` | Modality adapters | Factory callable returning configured adapter instance |
| `lobster.providers` | External data providers | Class (no-arg instantiation) |
| `lobster.download_services` | Download service classes | Class (no-arg instantiation) |
| `lobster.queue_preparers` | Queue preparation logic | Class (no-arg instantiation) |

Each domain package declares its agents in its `pyproject.toml`. For example, `lobster-transcriptomics` registers `transcriptomics_expert`, `annotation_expert`, and `de_analysis_expert`. The `AGENT_TO_PACKAGE` mapping in `component_registry.py` serves as a fallback — when an agent is referenced but its entry point isn't found (package not installed), the system can produce actionable install instructions.

The registry applies a **three-layer filter** before agents reach the graph: (1) explicit enable-list or workspace config, (2) auto-inclusion of child agents for enabled parents, and (3) subscription-tier gating. Agents that fail to load (missing dependencies, import errors) are pruned gracefully — the graph continues with whatever agents succeeded, logging install hints for the failures.

Sources: [component_registry.py](lobster/core/component_registry.py#L1-L72), [component_registry.py](lobster/core/component_registry.py#L86-L118), [plugin_loader.py](lobster/core/plugin_loader.py#L1-L79)

## Data Layer: DataManagerV2 and Modality Adapters

The `DataManagerV2` is the central orchestrator for all multi-omics data operations. It coordinates a stack of interchangeable components:

- **Modality Adapters** (`IModalityAdapter`) — domain-specific data handlers (TranscriptomicsAdapter, ProteomicsAdapter, MetabolomicsAdapter) that know how to load, validate, and transform data for their modality
- **Storage Backends** (`IDataBackend`) — persistence strategies (H5ADBackend for single-modal, MuDataBackend for multi-modal) that abstract file I/O
- **Provenance Tracker** — records every analysis step as Analysis IR (Intermediate Representation), enabling full lineage tracking and notebook export
- **Queue System** — download queue (with rate limiting) and publication queue for managing external data acquisition and result dissemination

DataManagerV2 supports **backed-mode loading** for large files (≥1 GB), loading AnnData in `backed='r'` mode to avoid OOM, with an explicit `materialize_modality()` call when mutation is needed. Plot management is integrated via `PlotManager`, and session persistence uses a `.lobster/sessions/<session_id>/` directory structure.

```
DataManagerV2
├── Adapters (IModalityAdapter)
│   ├── TranscriptomicsAdapter (scanpy-dependent)
│   ├── ProteomicsAdapter
│   ├── MetabolomicsAdapter
│   ├── ProteinStructureAdapter
│   └── PseudobulkAdapter
├── Backends (IDataBackend)
│   ├── H5ADBackend (.h5ad single-modality)
│   ├── H5ADModalityBackend (h5ad within mudata)
│   └── MuDataBackend (.h5mu multi-modality)
├── Provenance (Analysis IR)
│   ├── create_data_loading_ir() / create_data_saving_ir()
│   └── ProvenanceTracker
├── Queues
│   ├── DownloadQueue (rate-limited external data)
│   └── PublicationQueue (result dissemination)
└── PlotManager (Plotly figure lifecycle)
```

Sources: [data_manager.py](lobster/core/runtime/data_manager.py#L1-L65), [base_client.py](lobster/core/interfaces/base_client.py#L1-L182)

## Client Layer and Frontend Integration

Lobster exposes two client implementations, both conforming to the `BaseClient` abstract interface:

| Client | Location | Execution | Use Case |
|--------|----------|-----------|----------|
| `AgentClient` | `lobster.core.client` | Local — assembles graph in-process | CLI, local development |
| `CloudLobsterClient` | `lobster.lobster_cloud` | Remote — API calls to Lobster Cloud | SaaS, Go TUI |

The `BaseClient` ABC defines a uniform contract: `query()`, `get_status()`, `list_workspace_files()`, `read_file()`, `write_file()`, `get_conversation_history()`, `reset()`, `export_session()`, and optional `get_token_usage()`. This means the Python CLI and Go TUI can swap between local and cloud execution without changing their interaction logic.

The Python CLI (`lobster/cli.py`) is a Typer application with Rich terminal rendering. It handles Python version guarding (3.12+), lazy imports for fast startup (~5s saved), and prompt_toolkit autocomplete. Subcommands are organized in `cli_internal/commands/` with a "heavy/light" split — heavy modules (session infrastructure, extraction cache) are loaded lazily to keep initial startup fast.

Sources: [base_client.py](lobster/core/interfaces/base_client.py#L1-L182), [client.py](lobster/core/client.py#L1-L200), [cli.py](lobster/cli.py#L1-L90)

## Domain Packages Ecosystem

Domain packages are independently installable PyPI packages that plug into Lobster's core via entry points. Each package contributes one or more specialist agents, their associated state schemas, modality adapters, and provider integrations. The monorepo structure under `packages/` ensures cohesive development while allowing users to install only what they need.

| Package | Agents | Key Capabilities |
|---------|--------|-----------------|
| `lobster-transcriptomics` | transcriptomics_expert, annotation_expert, de_analysis_expert | scRNA-seq QC, clustering, cell annotation, differential expression |
| `lobster-proteomics` | proteomics_expert, proteomics_de_analysis_expert, biomarker_discovery_expert | Proteomics quantification, DE, biomarker identification |
| `lobster-genomics` | genomics_expert, variant_analysis_expert | Genomic data analysis, variant calling |
| `lobster-metabolomics` | metabolomics_expert | LC-MS metabolomics processing |
| `lobster-drug-discovery` | drug_discovery_expert, cheminformatics_expert, clinical_dev_expert, pharmacogenomics_expert | Drug design, ADMET, clinical development |
| `lobster-ml` | machine_learning_expert, feature_selection_expert, survival_analysis_expert | ML pipelines, feature engineering, survival modeling |
| `lobster-visualization` | visualization_expert_agent | Plotly-based scientific visualization |
| `lobster-structural-viz` | protein_structure_visualization_expert | 3D protein structure rendering |
| `lobster-metadata` | metadata_assistant | Dataset metadata extraction and validation |
| `lobster-research` | research_agent, data_expert_agent | Literature search, data discovery |

> [!TIP]
> When an agent is requested but its package isn't installed, the `AGENT_TO_PACKAGE` mapping enables the system to produce exact install commands (e.g., `uv pip install 'lobster-transcriptomics'`) rather than silent failures. This mapping is the single source of truth for the install-suggestion feature.

Sources: [component_registry.py](lobster/core/component_registry.py#L86-L118), [graph.py](lobster/agents/graph.py#L425-L535)

## Cross-Cutting Concerns

**Security Policy** is embedded directly in the supervisor prompt as the highest-priority section of an instruction hierarchy: security policy > system instructions > user messages > tool results > file content. This prevents prompt injection from external data sources (GEO, PubMed, PRIDE). Tool outputs are wrapped in `<tool_data>` markers for spotlighting.

**LLM Provider Configuration** is managed through a provider registry in `lobster/config/providers/`, with a factory function `create_llm()` that resolves provider + model from settings, workspace config, or explicit overrides. Supported providers include Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google Gemini, Ollama, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Azure, and Omics-OS Gateway.

**Subscription Tiers** gate agent availability. The `is_agent_available()` function checks the current tier (free/premium/enterprise) against agent-level tier requirements, and the graph construction pipeline filters out agents that exceed the user's tier.

Sources: [supervisor.py](lobster/agents/supervisor.py#L66-L106), [component_registry.py](lobster/core/component_registry.py#L120-L183)

- **Working with the agent graph?** → [Supervisor Agent and Routing](5-supervisor-agent-and-routing) for how the supervisor classifies requests and delegates, then [LangGraph State and Graph Topology](6-langgraph-state-and-graph-topology) for state flow details
- **Building a new agent or package?** → [Plugin System and Entry Points](8-plugin-system-and-entry-points) for the entry-point contract, then [Scaffold and Package Validation](10-scaffold-and-package-validation) for scaffolding tools
- **Integrating a new data modality?** → [DataManager and Modality Adapters](11-datamanager-and-modality-adapters) for the adapter interface, then [Provenance Tracking and IR](12-provenance-tracking-and-ir) for lineage requirements
- **Configuring providers or workspaces?** → [LLM Provider Configuration](17-llm-provider-configuration) or [Workspace and Session Management](18-workspace-and-session-management)
- **Understanding security?** → [Security Policy and Instruction Hierarchy](21-security-policy-and-instruction-hierarchy) for the full threat model and mitigation strategy

# Supervisor Agent and Routing



The supervisor agent is the central orchestrator in Lobster's multi-agent architecture — the single point of contact between the user and every specialist agent. Rather than routing through a complex graph topology, Lobster uses the **Tool Calling pattern**: the supervisor is a LangGraph `ReAct` agent whose "tools" are delegation functions that invoke sub-agents. This design makes routing a consequence of the LLM's own tool selection, driven by a dynamically assembled system prompt that encodes the agent directory, cognitive protocol, and orchestration principles. The result is a system where routing logic is declarative (expressed in prompt sections and tool descriptions) rather than imperative (hard-coded branching rules), letting the supervisor adapt its delegation strategy to context that changes at runtime.

## Architecture: The Tool Calling Supervisor

At the highest level, the supervisor sits at the center of a star topology. Every user message enters through the supervisor node; every specialist response flows back through it. The graph itself is deliberately simple — a single `StateGraph` with one node named `"supervisor"` connected from `START` to `END` — because all routing intelligence lives inside the supervisor's ReAct loop, not in graph edges.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph StateGraph
        START --> S[supervisor<br/>ReAct Agent]
        S --> END
    end

    S -.->|handoff_to_research_agent| RA["Research Agent()"]
    S -.->|handoff_to_data_expert_agent| DE["Data Expert Agent()"]
    S -.->|handoff_to_transcriptomics_expert| TE[Transcriptomics Expert]
    S -.->|handoff_to_metabolomics_expert| ME[Metabolomics Expert]
    S -.->|handoff_to_genomics_expert| GE[Genomics Expert]
    S -.->|execute_custom_code| CC[Custom Code Execution]
    S -.->|handoff_to_...| MORE[Other Domain Agents]

    TE -.->|handoff_to_annotation_expert| AE[Annotation Expert<br/>child of Transcriptomics]
    TE -.->|handoff_to_de_analysis_expert| DEA["DE Analysis Expert()<br/>child of Transcriptomics"]

    RA -.->|queue entry_id| DE
    S -.->|retrieve_agent_result| STORE[(InMemoryStore)]

    style S fill:#2563eb,stroke:#1e40af,color:#fff
    style TE fill:#7c3aed,stroke:#5b21b6,color:#fff
    style RA fill:#059669,stroke:#047857,color:#fff
    style DE fill:#d97706,stroke:#b45309,color:#fff
```

The graph construction happens in [`create_bioinformatics_graph()`](lobster/agents/graph.py#L678-L920), which returns a tuple of `(compiled_graph, GraphMetadata)`. The `GraphMetadata` dataclass exposes agent hierarchy, subscription tier, and supervisor-accessible agent names to frontends via a `to_dict()` serialization method — making the graph's configuration inspectable without re-compilation.

Sources: [graph.py](lobster/agents/graph.py#L860-L878), [graph.py](lobster/agents/graph.py#L678-L726)

## Prompt Assembly: Seven Sections, One Dynamic Prompt

The supervisor's behavior is controlled entirely by its system prompt, which is assembled at graph creation time by [`create_supervisor_prompt()`](lobster/agents/supervisor.py#L22-L63). This function stitches together seven section builders, each responsible for a distinct behavioral domain. The prompt is **dynamic** — it reflects the current data context, active agent list, and `SupervisorConfig` settings — meaning the same codebase produces different prompts for different configurations.

| Section Builder | Purpose | Dynamic? |
|---|---|---|
| `_build_security_policy()` | Immutable instruction hierarchy, content boundary rules, prohibited actions | No (static) |
| `_build_identity_section(config)` | Role definition, admin mode toggle | Yes (admin_mode) |
| `_build_cognitive_protocol()` | Request classification taxonomy (A/B/C/D), data inspection rule, parallel execution guidance | No (static) |
| `_build_agent_directory(active_agents, config)` | Tree-structured agent listing with routing keywords and download queue protocol | Yes (active agents, admin_mode) |
| `_build_orchestration_principles()` | Multi-step coordination, error handling, routing recovery, continuation rules | No (static) |
| `_build_response_behavior(config, interactive)` | Clarification limits, download confirmations, summarization style | Yes (all config fields, interactive flag) |
| `_build_agent_result_memory()` | Store key retrieval rules for accessing full sub-agent results | No (static) |
| `_build_live_context(data_manager, config)` | Loaded modality snapshot, system info, memory stats | Yes (runtime data) |

The security policy section enforces a strict **instruction hierarchy**: security rules > system instructions > user messages > tool results > file content. This is the foundation of Lobster's defense against prompt injection via untrusted data sources like GEO metadata or PubMed abstracts.

> [!TIP]
> The `_build_agent_directory` section is the routing backbone. It renders a tree showing parent→child relationships and injects **routing keywords** from `AgentRegistryConfig.routing_keywords` into each agent entry. These keywords, combined with the `handoff_tool_description` on each delegation tool, are what the LLM uses to select the correct agent — making routing accuracy depend on prompt engineering quality, not code logic.

Sources: [supervisor.py](lobster/agents/supervisor.py#L22-L63), [supervisor.py](lobster/agents/supervisor.py#L66-L106), [supervisor.py](lobster/agents/supervisor.py#L160-L235)

## Cognitive Protocol: The A/B/C/D Classification

Every incoming request passes through the supervisor's **Cognitive Protocol**, a four-way classification that determines the execution path:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    REQ[User Request] --> CLASSIFY{Classify Request}

    CLASSIFY -->|"(A) Direct Answer"| SELF[Supervisor responds<br/>directly]
    CLASSIFY -->|"(B) Single-Agent Task"| DELEGATE1[Delegate to one specialist<br/>with full context]
    CLASSIFY -->|"(C) Multi-Step Pipeline"| PLAN[Create todo plan<br/>with write_todos]
    PLAN --> STEP1[Execute step 1<br/>delegate to agent]
    STEP1 --> STEP2[Pass results as context<br/>execute step 2]
    STEP2 --> MORE_STEPS[...continue until<br/>all todos completed]
    CLASSIFY -->|"(D) No Agent Match"| CODE[Execute custom code<br/>as fallback]

    style CLASSIFY fill:#2563eb,stroke:#1e40af,color:#fff
    style PLAN fill:#7c3aed,stroke:#5b21b6,color:#fff
    style SELF fill:#059669,stroke:#047857,color:#fff
```

- **(A) Direct Answer**: Greetings, concept explanations, workspace lookups — the supervisor handles these without delegation.
- **(B) Single-Agent Task**: Clear domain mapping. The supervisor includes relevant data context (modality names, dimensions, prior steps) in its handoff message.
- **(C) Multi-Step Pipeline**: Two or more agents or three or more steps. The supervisor **must** create a todo plan via `write_todos` before delegating, then execute one step at a time, marking progress.
- **(D) No Agent Match**: Fallback to `execute_custom_code` for cross-modal analysis or tasks outside any agent's domain. Delegation is always attempted first.

Before delegating any analysis task, the protocol requires the supervisor to call `list_available_modalities` to understand what data is loaded — a guard against stale context in the system prompt snapshot.

Sources: [supervisor.py](lobster/agents/supervisor.py#L131-L157)

## Delegation: Tool Calling Pattern and Two Tool Factories

Lobster implements delegation through the **Tool Calling pattern** rather than LangGraph's Handoffs or Command/Send patterns. The supervisor sees each sub-agent as a named tool (e.g., `handoff_to_research_agent`) and invokes it with a `task_description` string. Two factory functions create these delegation tools, distinguished by when the agent reference is resolved:

| Factory | Resolution Time | Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| `_create_agent_tool()` | **Eager** — agent instance captured at creation | Supervisor → top-level agent handoffs |
| `_create_lazy_delegation_tool()` | **Lazy** — agent looked up from shared dict at invocation | Parent → child agent handoffs |

The lazy variant captures the `created_agents` dict **by reference** rather than by value. This is critical because child agents may not exist in the dict when the parent's delegation tools are created — the single-pass creation order means the dict is still being populated. At invocation time, the lazy tool looks up the agent by name; if missing, it returns an actionable install command from `AGENT_TO_PACKAGE`.

Both factories delegate to the shared async pipeline [`_invoke_and_store()`](lobster/agents/graph.py#L143-L186), which: (1) constructs a `RunnableConfig` with `run_name` and tags for callback attribution, (2) invokes the agent with a single user message containing the task description, (3) extracts the final message content, and (4) **dual-writes** the result to `InMemoryStore`, appending a `[store_key=...]` reference to the returned content. This store mechanism is what enables the `retrieve_agent_result` tool and the agent result memory system.

> [!TIP]
> The `created_agents` dict is mutated in-place by `_create_agents_single_pass()`. Lazy delegation tools capture this dict by reference and resolve agents at invocation time. **Never replace the dict object** — only add to it. Replacing the dict would orphan all lazy tool closures, causing every parent→child handoff to fail with "agent not available."

Sources: [graph.py](lobster/agents/graph.py#L189-L224), [graph.py](lobster/agents/graph.py#L227-L301), [graph.py](lobster/agents/graph.py#L394-L535)

## Agent Hierarchy and Access Control

Agents form a two-tier hierarchy: **supervisor-accessible** (top-level) and **child** (accessible only through their parent). The `AgentRegistryConfig.supervisor_accessible` field controls this:

- **`None` (default)**: Inferred from hierarchy — if an agent appears in any parent's `child_agents` list, it is NOT supervisor-accessible.
- **`True`**: Explicitly allow supervisor access, overriding inference.
- **`False`**: Explicitly deny supervisor access, overriding inference.

The function [`_resolve_worker_agents()`](lobster/agents/graph.py#L304-L391) applies three filters in sequence:

1. **Enabled agents filter**: `enabled_agents` parameter > `config.enabled_agents` > all discovered agents. Notably, `enabled_agents=[]` means zero agents (uses `is not None` check, not truthiness), while `config.enabled_agents=[]` means no preference.
2. **Child auto-inclusion**: If a parent is enabled, its children are automatically included even if not explicitly listed.
3. **Tier-based gating**: The `agent_filter` callable (defaulting to `is_agent_available(name, tier)`) excludes agents beyond the current subscription tier.

After resolution, `_build_supervisor_tools()` creates handoff tools only for supervisor-accessible agents, skipping children (who receive their tools via lazy delegation from their parent).

Sources: [graph.py](lobster/agents/graph.py#L304-L391), [graph.py](lobster/agents/graph.py#L538-L636), [agent_registry.py](lobster/agents/../../lobster/config/agent_registry.py#L17-L54)

## The Download Queue Coordination Protocol

One cross-agent pattern receives special treatment in the supervisor prompt: the **download queue protocol** between `research_agent` and `data_expert_agent`. When both agents are active, the agent directory section injects a coordination protocol:

```
1. research_agent prepares queue entry (validate_dataset_metadata or prepare_dataset_download)
2. Extract entry_id from response (format: queue_{accession}_{hex8})
3. Confirm with user before downloading (or proceed autonomously in admin mode)
4. handoff_to_data_expert_agent("execute_download_from_queue(entry_id=...)")
```

This producer-consumer pattern — where one agent creates a queue entry and another consumes it — is the canonical example of multi-step coordination. The protocol is conditionally injected only when both agents are present, and adapts to `admin_mode` by skipping the user confirmation step.

Sources: [supervisor.py](lobster/agents/supervisor.py#L216-L234)

## Orchestration Principles: Error Handling and Routing Recovery

The `<Orchestration Principles>` section encodes the supervisor's recovery and quality rules:

**Error handling**: One retry with corrected parameters for parameter errors; escalation to the user with actionable guidance for fundamental failures. Never retry in infinite loops.

**Routing recovery**: If an agent returns an error about unsupported data types or missing adapters, the supervisor re-checks the agent directory and tries the correct domain expert. Maximum one re-route attempt per request.

**Continuation on tool error**: When a sub-agent's code execution fails, the supervisor does NOT re-route to a different agent for the same analytical task. The same agent retries with corrected defensive code. If re-delegating to the same agent after a failed step in a multi-step protocol, the supervisor instructs it to continue from the failed step — **never restart from step 1**.

**Response quality**: Every response must include key findings, metrics, and file names in 2–4 sentences. The supervisor suggests logical next steps and never returns empty acknowledgments.

Sources: [supervisor.py](lobster/agents/supervisor.py#L238-L270)

## Context Management: Budget, Trimming, and Store-Backed Memory

The supervisor operates under a strict context budget to prevent token overflow across all LLM providers. The [`resolve_context_budget()`](lobster/agents/context_management.py#L117-L168) function calculates the usable token budget as:

```
budget = context_window × 0.80 − tool_schema_tokens − system_prompt_tokens
```

The 20% reserve accounts for model output and safety margin against token counting drift. Tool schemas are measured explicitly via [`measure_tool_schema_tokens()`](lobster/agents/context_management.py#L88-L114) because they are sent with every LLM call but not counted by `trim_messages` — a subtle source of context overflow that a naive "85% of window" approach would miss.

The [`create_supervisor_pre_model_hook()`](lobster/agents/context_management.py#L396) factory creates a hook that runs on each ReAct iteration. It performs three operations in sequence:

1. **Store key injection**: Reads all stored agent results from `InMemoryStore` and appends a `<Available Stored Results>` section to the system message, ensuring the LLM always knows which results it can retrieve.
2. **Message trimming**: Uses LangChain's `trim_messages` with the resolved budget, applying a `strategy="last"` to keep the most recent conversation turns.
3. **Tool result spotlighting**: Wraps all `ToolMessage` content in `<tool_data>...</tool_data>` markers, ensuring the LLM treats tool output as data rather than instructions.
