# Scaffold and Package Validation



Lobster's plugin architecture demands structural rigor: every domain package must conform to a precise contract governing namespace layout, entry point wiring, agent factory signatures, and AQUADIF metadata. The **scaffold** system generates structurally correct packages from Jinja2 templates, while the **validation** system enforces contract compliance through both static AST analysis and runtime contract test mixins. Together, they form a closed loop — scaffold produces structure, validation certifies it — ensuring that no plugin, whether generated or hand-written, drifts from the canonical pattern.

Sources: [__init__.py](lobster/scaffold/__init__.py#L1-L19), [validators.py](lobster/scaffold/validators.py#L1-L38)

## The Scaffold-to-Validation Lifecycle

The lifecycle of a compliant plugin follows a deterministic path: scaffold generates the package skeleton → the author implements domain logic → static validation checks structural invariants → runtime contract tests verify behavioral compliance. This two-phase validation model catches different classes of defects: static checks catch *structural* violations (missing files, wrong entry points, misplaced config) without importing any code, while runtime contract tests catch *semantic* violations (missing tool metadata, provenance disconnects, bare collection types) by actually invoking the factory.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["lobster scaffold agent<br/>--name epigenomics_expert"] --> B["Generated Package<br/>lobster-epigenomics/"]
    B --> C["Author Implements<br/>Domain Logic"]
    C --> D["lobster validate-plugin<br/>lobster-epigenomics"]
    D --> E{"8 Static Checks<br/>Pass?"}
    E -- No --> F["Fix Structural<br/>Violations"]
    F --> D
    E -- Yes --> G["pytest -m contract<br/>Runtime Tests"]
    G --> H{"Contract Tests<br/>Pass?"}
    H -- No --> I["Fix Behavioral<br/>Violations"]
    I --> G
    H -- Yes --> J["✓ Compliant Plugin<br/>Ready to Publish"]
```

The separation is deliberate: static validation runs in milliseconds against raw source files with zero dependency imports, making it suitable for CI pre-commit hooks and IDE integration. Runtime contract tests execute the factory with mocked dependencies, making them slower but capable of detecting metadata-runtime disconnects that pure AST analysis cannot.

Sources: [validators.py](lobster/scaffold/validators.py#L40-L65), [contract_mixins.py](lobster/testing/contract_mixins.py#L1-L50)

## Scaffold Generator: Producing the Canonical Package

The `scaffold_agent` function generates a complete, structurally correct plugin package from a Jinja2 template set. It resolves templates via `importlib.resources` for robustness across namespace packages, wheels, and zip installs — never relying on `__file__` traversal. The generator accepts a core parameter set and derives all naming conventions automatically: `_derive_domain` strips the `_expert` suffix to produce the domain directory name, and `_to_class_name` converts snake_case to PascalCase for state class names.

| Parameter | Purpose | Example |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| `name` | Agent name in snake_case | `"epigenomics_expert"` |
| `display_name` | Human-readable label | `"Epigenomics Expert"` |
| `description` | Capability description | `"Epigenomics data analysis"` |
| `tier` | Subscription tier | `"free"`, `"premium"`, `"enterprise"` |
| `children` | Optional child agent names | `["methylation_expert"]` |
| `output_dir` | Target directory | `Path(".")` |

The generator produces the following directory structure, strictly adhering to PEP 420 namespace package rules — note the deliberate absence of `__init__.py` at `lobster/` and `lobster/agents/` levels:

```
lobster-{domain}/
├── pyproject.toml              # Entry points + namespace config
├── README.md
├── lobster/                    # ← NO __init__.py (PEP 420)
│   └── agents/                 # ← NO __init__.py (PEP 420)
│       └── {domain}/
│           ├── __init__.py     # State exports only, no ImportError guards
│           ├── {agent_name}.py # AGENT_CONFIG + factory function
│           ├── shared_tools.py # AQUADIF-categorized tool factory
│           ├── state.py        # Inherits AgentState
│           ├── config.py       # Platform/domain config dataclass
│           ├── prompts.py      # Prompt factory function
│           └── py.typed        # PEP 561 marker
└── tests/
    ├── __init__.py
    ├── test_contract.py        # AgentContractTestMixin subclass
    └── conftest.py             # Mock fixtures
```

When `children` is provided, the generator renders additional `agent.py.j2` files for each child agent within the same domain directory, inheriting the parent's context but with `is_child: True` and `has_children: False`. This co-location pattern keeps related agents discoverable under a single domain namespace.

> [!TIP]
> Never manually add `__init__.py` at `lobster/` or `lobster/agents/` — this violates PEP 420 and will be caught by validation Check 1. The namespace package mechanism relies on these directories being *implicit* namespaces discovered by `setuptools.find` with `namespaces=true` in `pyproject.toml`.

Sources: [agent.py](lobster/scaffold/generators/agent.py#L1-L136), [pyproject.toml.j2](lobster/scaffold/templates/pyproject.toml.j2#L1-L45), [PATTERNS.md](lobster/scaffold/PATTERNS.md#L1-L52)

## Template Anatomy: The Agent Module Contract

The `agent.py.j2` template encodes the most critical structural rule in the plugin contract: **AGENT_CONFIG must appear before heavy imports**. This is not a style preference — it is a performance contract. The agent registry discovers plugins by loading entry point modules, and if AGENT_CONFIG is buried below `langgraph` or `langchain` imports, discovery latency explodes from <50ms to several seconds per agent. The template enforces this by placing only a single lightweight import (`from lobster.config.agent_registry import AgentRegistryConfig`) before the AGENT_CONFIG assignment, with all heavy imports below a visible separator comment.

The factory function generated by the template follows a strict signature contract. The five **standard parameters** — `data_manager`, `callback_handler`, `agent_name`, `delegation_tools`, and `workspace_path` — are required by the plugin system and validated by both static and runtime checks. Additional parameters like `provider_override`, `model_override`, and `store` are permitted extensions. The factory's internal flow is: lazy-import the prompt → configure LLM via `create_llm` → instantiate tools via `create_shared_tools` → compile a `create_react_agent` graph with the assembled components.

The `shared_tools.py.j2` template generates the AQUADIF-compliant tool factory. Each tool is defined as a `@tool`-decorated function inside the `create_shared_tools` closure, with access to `data_manager` and injected services. The template provides four canonical tool categories — IMPORT, QUALITY, ANALYZE, UTILITY — each with a provenance `AnalysisStep` IR object and a `log_tool_usage(ir=ir)` call. This is the provenance contract made concrete: every tool that declares `provenance: True` must construct an `AnalysisStep` and pass it to `data_manager.log_tool_usage`.

> [!TIP]
> The `prompt=` parameter in `create_react_agent` is the correct keyword — **not** `state_modifier=`. Using `state_modifier` is a common migration error from older LangGraph versions. The factory also uses lazy prompt import (`from lobster.agents.{domain}.prompts import ...` inside the factory body) so that AGENT_CONFIG discovery succeeds even before the prompts module exists.

Sources: [agent.py.j2](lobster/scaffold/templates/agent.py.j2#L1-L118), [shared_tools.py.j2](lobster/scaffold/templates/shared_tools.py.j2#L1-L200), [PATTERNS.md](lobster/scaffold/PATTERNS.md#L23-L52)

## Static Validation: Eight Structural Checks

The `validate_plugin` function in `lobster/scaffold/validators.py` performs eight ordered checks against a plugin directory, returning a list of `ValidationResult` dataclasses. Each result carries a `check` name, `passed` boolean, human-readable `message`, and `severity` (default `"error"`, optionally `"warning"`). The checks are ordered by severity — structural violations that would prevent the plugin from loading at all come first, followed by contract violations that would cause runtime errors.

| # | Check | What It Catches | Severity |
|---|-------|-----------------|----------|
| 1 | **PEP 420 compliance** | `__init__.py` at `lobster/` or `lobster/agents/` — breaks namespace package resolution | Error |
| 2 | **Entry points** | Missing `lobster.agents` group in `pyproject.toml`, or entry point value not ending with `:AGENT_CONFIG` | Error |
| 3 | **AGENT_CONFIG position** | AGENT_CONFIG assigned after `langgraph`/`langchain` imports — defeats fast discovery | Error |
| 4 | **Factory signature** | Factory function missing standard parameters (`data_manager`, `callback_handler`, `agent_name`, `delegation_tools`, `workspace_path`) | Error |
| 5 | **AQUADIF metadata** | `@tool` definitions without `.metadata` assignments — breaks tool categorization | Error |
| 6 | **Provenance calls** | Tools declaring `provenance: True` but not calling `log_tool_usage(ir=ir)` — metadata-runtime disconnect | Error |
| 7 | **Import boundaries** | Cross-agent imports from other domains — violates plugin isolation | Error |
| 8 | **No ImportError guard** | `try/except ImportError` in domain `__init__.py` — contradicts entry-point-based discovery | Error |

### Check Mechanics in Detail

**Check 1 (PEP 420)** simply tests for the existence of `lobster/__init__.py` and `lobster/agents/__init__.py`. These files must not exist because `lobster` and `lobster.agents` are implicit namespace packages shared across all installed plugins; an explicit `__init__.py` would short-circuit namespace resolution and hide other packages' contributions.

**Check 3 (AGENT_CONFIG position)** uses Python's `ast` module to walk the parsed syntax tree of each agent module. It locates the `AGENT_CONFIG` assignment node and the earliest `ast.Import` or `ast.ImportFrom` node referencing `langgraph` or `langchain` modules. If the config line number exceeds the heavy import line number, the check fails. Non-agent modules (like `shared_tools.py`, `state.py`, `config.py`, `prompts.py`) are skipped since they don't define `AGENT_CONFIG`.

**Check 6 (Provenance calls)** delegates to the shared `has_provenance_call` function from `lobster.config.aquadif` — a deliberate design choice noted as "Delta 1" in the source to avoid reimplementing the AST walk logic. This function checks whether `log_tool_usage(ir=ir)` appears in the AST, ensuring that the provenance flag declared in metadata actually corresponds to runtime provenance tracking.

**Check 7 (Import boundaries)** uses a regex pattern to detect `from lobster.agents.{other_domain}.{module} import` statements where `{other_domain}` differs from the current plugin's domain. This enforces plugin isolation: domain packages must communicate through the supervisor's delegation tools, not by directly importing each other's internals.

**Check 8 (No ImportError guard)** walks the AST of each domain's `__init__.py` looking for `except ImportError`, `except (..., ImportError)`, or bare `except` handlers. The `try/except ImportError` pattern is a legacy anti-pattern from when agent discovery relied on eager imports; the entry-point mechanism makes it unnecessary and harmful (it silently swallows real import errors during development).

Sources: [validators.py](lobster/scaffold/validators.py#L1-L520)

## Runtime Contract Testing: AgentContractTestMixin

While static validation operates on source files without importing them, `AgentContractTestMixin` performs runtime verification by actually importing the plugin, calling its factory with mocked dependencies, and inspecting the resulting graph and tool objects. It is the authoritative runtime contract enforcer, covering 13 distinct test methods organized into three phases.

### Phase 1: Plugin Contract Tests

These tests verify the structural API that the supervisor and registry depend on:

- **`test_factory_has_standard_params`** — Inspects the factory's `inspect.signature` and asserts all five standard parameters are present. Missing parameters cause the supervisor to fail at graph construction time.
- **`test_no_deprecated_handoff_tools`** — Catches the renamed parameter: `handoff_tools` → `delegation_tools` (Phase 2 rename for semantic clarity).
- **`test_agent_config_exists`** — Verifies `AGENT_CONFIG` is defined at module top level.
- **`test_agent_config_has_name`** and **`test_agent_config_has_tier_requirement`** — Validate the two mandatory `AgentRegistryConfig` fields.

### Phase 2: AQUADIF Contract Tests

These tests enforce the AQUADIF tool taxonomy and provenance contract:

| Test ID | Test Method | What It Validates |
|---------|-------------|-------------------|
| TEST-02 | `test_tools_have_aquadif_metadata` | Every tool has `.metadata` with `categories` and `provenance` keys |
| TEST-03 | `test_categories_are_valid` | All category strings map to `AquadifCategory` enum members |
| TEST-04 | `test_categories_capped_at_three` | No tool exceeds 3 categories |
| TEST-05 | `test_provenance_tools_have_flag` | Tools with provenance-required primary categories declare `provenance: True` |
| TEST-06 | `test_minimum_viable_parent` | Parent agents provide IMPORT + QUALITY + (ANALYZE or DELEGATE) |
| TEST-07 | `test_metadata_objects_are_unique` | No two tools share the same metadata dict object reference |
| TEST-08 | `test_provenance_ast_validation` | Tools declaring `provenance: True` actually call `log_tool_usage(ir=ir)` |
| TEST-09 | `test_provenance_categories_not_buried` | Provenance-required categories aren't hidden behind non-provenance primaries |

### Phase 3: Schema Compatibility Tests

- **`test_tool_params_no_bare_collections`** — Detects bare `list`, `dict`, `tuple`, `set` type hints in tool parameters. Unparameterized collections produce JSON schemas without `items`/`properties` fields, triggering `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` on Gemini API. The fix is always to use parameterized types: `list[str]`, `dict[str, Any]`, etc.

### The Provenance Integrity Guarantee

The most sophisticated contract test is `test_provenance_ast_validation` (TEST-08), which directly addresses a Phase 1 evaluation finding: **100% of agents copied provenance boilerplate mechanically without adjusting based on metadata flags**. This test closes the gap by parsing the actual source code of each tool function via `inspect.getsource`, building an AST, and verifying that `log_tool_usage(ir=ir)` appears when `provenance: True` is declared. It uses the shared `has_provenance_call` function from `lobster.config.aquadif` — the same function used by static validation Check 6 — ensuring consistency between the two validation paths.

Similarly, `test_provenance_categories_not_buried` (TEST-09) prevents a subtle evasion: reordering categories to place a non-provenance primary (like UTILITY) ahead of a provenance-required secondary (like IMPORT). The rule is strict — if *any* category in the list requires provenance, the primary (first) category must also require provenance. This prevents gaming by reordering categories to dodge the provenance validation.

### Configuring the Mixin

To use `AgentContractTestMixin`, a test class must define `agent_module` and `factory_name` as class variables. The scaffold generator produces a ready-to-use test file via `test_contract.py.j2`:

```python
@pytest.mark.contract
class TestEpigenomicsExpertContract(AgentContractTestMixin):
    agent_module = "lobster.agents.epigenomics.epigenomics_expert"
    factory_name = "epigenomics_expert"
    is_parent_agent = False
    expected_tier = "free"
    tools_required = False  # Set True once factory produces working tools
```

The `tools_required` flag controls how the mixin handles empty tool lists. When `False` (the scaffold default), empty tools trigger a `pytest.skip`. When `True`, empty tools cause a hard failure — use this once your factory is fully implemented. The `is_parent_agent` flag gates `test_minimum_viable_parent`, which is skipped for leaf agents.

Sources: [contract_mixins.py](lobster/testing/contract_mixins.py#L1-L820), [test_contract.py.j2](lobster/scaffold/templates/test_contract.py.j2#L1-L27)

## The Validation-to-Scaffold Feedback Loop

When validation fails, the error messages are designed to point directly at the scaffold pattern that was violated. For example, Check 8's failure message reads: `"except ImportError at line {n} — use entry points for agent discovery"`. This is not generic advice — it references the specific architectural decision documented in `PATTERNS.md` and enforced by the `__init__.py.j2` template, which contains the comment: *"Do NOT use try/except ImportError here — see creating-agents.md."*

The `PATTERNS.md` file serves as the canonical reference document, verified against `packages/lobster-metabolomics/` as the golden package. It specifies exact line positions (AGENT_CONFIG at line 14), required field names, and naming conventions that both the templates and validators are synchronized against. The source code contains an explicit sync note in `validators.py`: *"Standalone equivalent at skills/lobster-dev/scripts/validate_plugin.py — keep checks aligned"*, indicating that a standalone CLI script mirrors these checks for use outside the Python runtime.

Sources: [PATTERNS.md](lobster/scaffold/PATTERNS.md#L1-L52), [validators.py](lobster/scaffold/validators.py#L35-L37), [__init__.py.j2](lobster/scaffold/templates/__init__.py.j2#L1-L8)

## Real-World Package Structure

Examining the reference package `lobster-metabolomics` reveals the mature form of a scaffolded plugin after domain logic has been implemented. Beyond the standard scaffold files, it adds a `services/` directory with three stateless service modules — `analysis`, `annotation`, and `quality` — each containing a single service class. These services are injected into `create_shared_tools` as parameters, following the closure-over-dependencies pattern that the scaffold template anticipates with its `# TODO: Add your stateless service parameters here` placeholders.

```
lobster-metabolomics/lobster/
├── agents/
│   └── metabolomics/
│       ├── __init__.py           # State export only
│       ├── metabolomics_expert.py # AGENT_CONFIG + factory
│       ├── shared_tools.py       # Tool factory with services
│       ├── prompts.py
│       ├── config.py
│       ├── state.py
│       └── py.typed
└── services/
    ├── analysis/
    │   └── metabolomics_analysis_service.py
    ├── annotation/
    │   └── metabolomics_annotation_service.py
    └── quality/
        ├── metabolomics_preprocessing_service.py
        └── metabolomics_quality_service.py
```

This separation between agents and services is architecturally significant: agents are *orchestration* (they compose tools and prompt LLMs), while services are *computation* (they execute domain algorithms). Keeping them in separate module trees ensures that services can be tested independently and that the agent module remains lightweight enough for fast entry point discovery.

Sources: [package structure](packages/lobster-metabolomics/lobster), [shared_tools.py.j2](lobster/scaffold/templates/shared_tools.py.j2#L34-L40)

## Testing Infrastructure: Mocks and Fixtures

The `lobster.testing` module provides shared infrastructure that eliminates duplication across package test suites. The public API includes `MockDataManager` (in-memory `DataManagerV2` with `add_modality` support), `MockLLM` (configurable response sequences), `MockProvenanceTracker` (IR capture), and `AgentContractTestMixin`. The `contract_mixins.py` itself uses `MockDataManager` and `MockLLM` internally when calling factories, patching `create_llm` at both the definition site (`lobster.config.llm_factory.create_llm`) and the factory's module path to handle both `from X import create_llm` and `X.create_llm()` call patterns.

The `fixtures.py` module provides `create_test_workspace` (generates the standard `data/`, `exports/`, `cache/`, `plots/` directory structure) and synthetic data generators: `synthetic_single_cell_data` (negative binomial counts with configurable sparsity, cell type annotations, and QC metrics), `synthetic_bulk_rnaseq_data` (higher counts with balanced experimental design), and `synthetic_proteomics_data`. These generators produce `AnnData` objects that are compatible with `MockDataManager.add_modality`, enabling end-to-end testing from data loading through analysis without requiring real datasets.

Sources: [__init__.py](lobster/testing/__init__.py#L1-L53), [fixtures.py](lobster/testing/fixtures.py#L1-L200), [contract_mixins.py](lobster/testing/contract_mixins.py#L206-L259)

## Navigating the Validation Landscape

The scaffold and validation systems sit within the broader extensibility subsystem. The scaffold generator produces packages that declare entry points consumed by the [Plugin System and Entry Points](8-plugin-system-and-entry-points) mechanism, and the AQUADIF metadata validated here is classified by the [AQUADIF Tool Taxonomy](9-aquadif-tool-taxonomy). Once a plugin passes validation, its tools are discoverable by the [Agent Registry and Discovery](7-agent-registry-and-discovery) system, and its provenance IR is tracked by the [Provenance Tracking and IR](12-provenance-tracking-and-ir) pipeline. For the end-to-end agent implementation patterns that validated packages must follow, see [Transcriptomics and Genomics Agents](14-transcriptomics-and-genomics-agents) and [Proteomics and Metabolomics Agents](15-proteomics-and-metabolomics-agents).

# DataManager and Modality Adapters



The **DataManagerV2** is Lobster's central orchestration layer for multi-omics data lifecycle management. It coordinates modality adapters, storage backends, and validation into a unified interface that transforms heterogeneous biological data — from single-cell RNA-seq matrices to protein crystal structures — into standardized `AnnData` objects with schema enforcement, provenance tracking, and automatic workspace persistence. Every data flow in Lobster, whether triggered by an agent tool or a CLI command, converges through this layer before reaching downstream analysis.

## Architectural Overview

The data management subsystem follows a three-tier architecture: **Adapters** convert raw files into canonical `AnnData` objects, **Backends** handle persistence to storage media, and the **DataManagerV2** orchestrates both while managing workspace state, provenance, and thread safety. This separation ensures that adding support for a new omics modality requires only a new adapter class — no changes to the orchestration or persistence logic.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Data Sources"
        CSV["CSV / TSV"]
        H5AD["H5AD"]
        PDB["PDB / mmCIF"]
        EXCEL["Excel"]
        PARQUET["Parquet"]
        DF["pd.DataFrame"]
    end

    subgraph "Modality Adapters (IModalityAdapter)"
        TA["TranscriptomicsAdapter"]
        PA["ProteomicsAdapter"]
        MA["MetabolomicsAdapter"]
        PSA["ProteinStructureAdapter"]
        PBKA["PseudobulkAdapter"]
        GA["Genomics Adapters<br/>(VCF / PLINK)"]
    end

    subgraph "DataManagerV2"
        REG["Adapter Registry"]
        MOD["Modality Store<br/>Dict[str, AnnData]"]
        PROV["Provenance Tracker"]
        WS["Workspace Manager<br/>+ Auto-Scan"]
    end

    subgraph "Storage Backends (IDataBackend)"
        H5B["H5ADBackend"]
        MDB["MuDataBackend"]
    end

    CSV & H5AD & PDB & EXCEL & PARQUET & DF --> TA & PA & MA & PSA & PBKA & GA
    TA & PA & MA & PSA & PBKA & GA --> REG
    REG --> MOD
    MOD --> PROV
    MOD --> H5B & MDB
    WS --> MOD
```

Sources: [data_manager.py](lobster/core/runtime/data_manager.py#L260-L399), [adapter.py](lobster/core/interfaces/adapter.py#L19-L103)

## The IModalityAdapter Contract

All modality adapters implement the `IModalityAdapter` abstract base class, which defines the contract for converting raw data into schema-enforced `AnnData` objects. The interface enforces four abstract methods — `from_source`, `validate`, `get_schema`, and `get_supported_formats` — while providing default implementations for format detection, preprocessing, quality metrics, metadata standardization, and provenance annotation. This design means that every adapter, regardless of biological domain, produces data that conforms to the same structural contract.

| Method | Purpose | Return Type |
|---|---|---|
| `from_source(source, **kwargs)` | Convert raw data to AnnData | `anndata.AnnData` |
| `validate(adata, strict)` | Validate against modality schema | `ValidationResult` |
| `get_schema()` | Declare required/optional obs, var, layers, uns | `Dict[str, Any]` |
| `get_supported_formats()` | List supported file extensions | `List[str]` |
| `get_modality_name()` | Return domain name (e.g., "transcriptomics") | `str` |
| `detect_format(source)` | Auto-detect file format from extension | `Optional[str]` |
| `preprocess_data(adata, **kwargs)` | Apply modality-specific preprocessing | `anndata.AnnData` |
| `get_quality_metrics(adata)` | Compute sparsity, memory, dimensions | `Dict[str, Any]` |
| `add_provenance(adata, source_info)` | Attach source tracking to `uns` | `anndata.AnnData` |

The `detect_format` method maps 11 file extensions (`.csv`, `.tsv`, `.txt`, `.h5ad`, `.h5`, `.xlsx`, `.xls`, `.mtx`, `.h5mu`, `.parquet`, `.loom`) to normalized format names, while `add_provenance` appends a timestamped dictionary to `adata.uns["provenance"]` capturing the adapter class, modality, source info, and processing parameters.

Sources: [adapter.py](lobster/core/interfaces/adapter.py#L19-L232)

## BaseAdapter: Shared Ingestion Infrastructure

The `BaseAdapter` provides the concrete scaffolding that all domain-specific adapters inherit from. It implements the common ingestion pipeline — loading data from files or DataFrames, converting to `AnnData`, enforcing numeric matrices, adding basic QC metadata, and filtering internal kwargs before they reach pandas. This eliminates substantial boilerplate; subclasses override only the modality-specific parsing and schema logic.

**File loading** is handled by four private methods, each with automatic delimiter detection and kwargs sanitization:

| Method | Formats | Key Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `_load_csv_data(path, sep, ...)` | CSV, TSV, TXT | Auto-detects tab vs. comma; filters `_LOBSTER_INTERNAL_KWARGS` |
| `_load_excel_data(path, sheet_name, ...)` | XLSX, XLS | Selects sheet; same kwargs filtering |
| `_load_parquet_data(path, ...)` | Parquet | Validates `pyarrow` availability with install hint |
| `_load_h5ad_data(path)` | H5AD | Direct `anndata.read_h5ad` with shape logging |

The `_LOBSTER_INTERNAL_KWARGS` frozenset (containing keys like `adapter`, `dataset_id`, `orientation`, `protein_id_col`, `transpose`, etc.) is critical: it prevents Lobster-orchestration parameters from leaking into pandas `read_csv` calls, which would raise `TypeError` on unexpected keyword arguments. Subclasses extend this set with their own domain-specific keys.

**The DataFrame-to-AnnData conversion** (`_create_anndata_from_dataframe`) implements several pragmatic heuristics: it strips non-numeric columns with a warning, converts to `float32`, automatically converts to sparse CSR format when sparsity exceeds 80% on matrices larger than 10,000 elements, and enforces unique variable names via `var_names_make_unique()` — a necessity for real-world datasets where gene symbols may be duplicated.

> [!TIP]
> The `_ensure_numeric_matrix` method deliberately **preserves NaN values** rather than coercing them to zero. In proteomics and metabolomics, NaN represents "below detection limit" (MNAR — missing not at random), and replacing with zero corrupts downstream differential expression and imputation. Domain adapters handle NaN via appropriate modality-specific strategies.

Sources: [base.py](lobster/core/adapters/base.py#L23-L399)

## Domain-Specific Adapters

Each adapter specializes the `BaseAdapter` pipeline for a particular biological domain, adding schema validation, domain-specific QC thresholds, and preprocessing logic. The following table summarizes the full adapter catalog and their distinguishing characteristics:

| Adapter | `data_type` Options | Default Transpose | Missing Value Strategy | Schema Module |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **TranscriptomicsAdapter** | `single_cell`, `bulk` | `True` (genes as rows) | N/A (zeros are valid) | `TranscriptomicsSchema` |
| **ProteomicsAdapter** | `mass_spectrometry`, `affinity` | `False` | `keep`, `fill_zero`, `drop` | `ProteomicsSchema` |
| **MetabolomicsAdapter** | `lc_ms`, `gc_ms`, `nmr` | `False` | `keep`, `fill_zero`, `drop` | `MetabolomicsSchema` |
| **PseudobulkAdapter** | (single type) | `False` | N/A | `TranscriptomicsSchema` (pseudobulk) |
| **ProteinStructureAdapter** | (single type) | N/A | N/A | `ProteinStructureSchema` |
| **VCFAdapter** | (genomics_wgs) | N/A | N/A | Genomics schema |
| **PLINKAdapter** | (genomics_snp_array) | N/A | N/A | Genomics schema |

### TranscriptomicsAdapter

The transcriptomics adapter handles both single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. It uses a lazy `scanpy` import for 10X matrix loading (`.mtx` format), provides a dedicated `from_quantification_dataframe` method for Kallisto/Salmon output, and enforces QC thresholds from `TranscriptomicsSchema`. The adapter separates metadata fields from processing parameters in `from_source`, storing non-processing kwargs into `adata.uns` after sanitization for H5AD compatibility. [transcriptomics_adapter.py](lobster/core/adapters/transcriptomics_adapter.py#L46-L177)

### ProteomicsAdapter

Proteomics data presents unique challenges: missing values are semantically meaningful (below detection limit), and orientation varies by source tool. The adapter supports an explicit `orientation` kwarg (`"features_as_rows"`, `"features_as_cols"`, or `"unknown"`) for auto-detection, and a `handle_missing_values` strategy parameter. The `_handle_missing_values` method respects the chosen strategy, with `"keep"` as the default to preserve MNAR structure for downstream imputation. [proteomics_adapter.py](lobster/core/adapters/proteomics_adapter.py#L24-L200)

### MetabolomicsAdapter

The metabolomics adapter supports LC-MS, GC-MS, and NMR platforms. It implements `_separate_intensity_metadata_columns` for auto-detecting which DataFrame columns contain intensity values versus metabolite metadata, and `_standardize_metabolomics_metadata` for normalizing column names across different instrument software conventions. [metabolomics_adapter.py](lobster/core/adapters/metabolomics_adapter.py#L24-L198)

### PseudobulkAdapter

The pseudobulk adapter reuses `TranscriptomicsSchema` with the `"pseudobulk"` schema type and adds `_parse_pseudobulk_sample_ids` to decompose sample identifiers following the `{sample_id}_{cell_type}` convention into structured `obs` metadata. It supports `aggregation_metadata` and `original_dataset_info` kwargs that attach single-cell derivation context to the pseudobulk AnnData. [pseudobulk_adapter.py](lobster/core/adapters/pseudobulk_adapter.py#L25-L194)

### ProteinStructureAdapter

The most architecturally distinct adapter, `ProteinStructureAdapter` converts Bio.PDB `Structure` objects into `AnnData` where **atoms are observations** and coordinates are variables. It uses `PDBParser` or `MMCIFParser` depending on file extension, supports NMR multi-model selection via `model_number`, and provides `include_hetero`/`include_waters` filtering. [protein_structure_adapter.py](lobster/core/adapters/protein_structure_adapter.py#L24-L179)

Sources: [transcriptomics_adapter.py](lobster/core/adapters/transcriptomics_adapter.py#L1-L177), [proteomics_adapter.py](lobster/core/adapters/proteomics_adapter.py#L1-L200), [metabolomics_adapter.py](lobster/core/adapters/metabolomics_adapter.py#L1-L198), [pseudobulk_adapter.py](lobster/core/adapters/pseudobulk_adapter.py#L1-L194), [protein_structure_adapter.py](lobster/core/adapters/protein_structure_adapter.py#L1-L179)

## DataManagerV2: The Orchestration Layer

`DataManagerV2` is the single entry point for all data operations in Lobster. It holds the adapter registry, the modality store, backend references, provenance tracker, workspace state, and download/publication queues. Its constructor accepts six configuration parameters that govern behavior across all subsystems:

| Parameter | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default_backend` | `"h5ad"` | Storage backend for save operations |
| `workspace_path` | Resolved via `resolve_workspace()` | Root directory; resolution: explicit > `LOBSTER_WORKSPACE` env > `cwd/.lobster_workspace` |
| `enable_provenance` | `True` | Enable `ProvenanceTracker` and IR recording |
| `session_dir` | `None` | Directory for persisted provenance (survives restarts) |
| `auto_scan` | `True` | Auto-load existing H5AD/tabular files from workspace |
| `backed_mode` | `False` | Enable backed-mode for H5AD files >1GB (also via `LOBSTER_BACKED_MODE=1`) |

### Adapter Registration: Two-Phase Discovery

Adapter registration follows a two-phase strategy. **Phase 1** discovers adapters from entry points via `component_registry.list_adapters()`, allowing plugin packages to contribute adapters without modifying core code. **Phase 2** registers hardcoded fallback adapters — but only for names not already claimed by Phase 1. This ensures that plugin-provided adapters take precedence while core adapters fill gaps.

```python
# Phase 1: Entry-point discovery (plugins first)
for name, adapter_factory in component_registry.list_adapters().items():
    adapter = adapter_factory()
    self.register_adapter(name, adapter)

# Phase 2: Hardcoded fallbacks (only if not already registered)
if "transcriptomics_single_cell" not in self.adapters:
    self.register_adapter("transcriptomics_single_cell",
        TranscriptomicsAdapter(data_type="single_cell"))
```

The default registration creates six adapter instances: `transcriptomics_single_cell`, `transcriptomics_bulk`, `proteomics_ms`, `proteomics_affinity`, `genomics_wgs` (VCF), and `genomics_snp_array` (PLINK) — with proteomics and genomics conditionally registered based on optional dependency availability.

Sources: [data_manager.py](lobster/core/runtime/data_manager.py#L269-L590)

### Workspace Auto-Loading and File Resolution

When `auto_scan=True`, the DataManager scans the `workspace/data/` directory on initialization, loading files in a prioritized two-phase sequence: H5AD files first (they take precedence over same-stem tabular files), then tabular files. The system applies size guards — H5AD files >4GB are skipped (with a suggestion to use `load_modality` explicitly), and tabular files >500MB are skipped due to memory expansion concerns. Corrupted autosave files are silently cleaned up; corrupted regular files are logged as warnings.

The `_resolve_adapter_for_file` method determines which adapter handles a given file extension. H5AD files bypass the adapter system entirely (loaded directly via `anndata.read_h5ad` for speed). When exactly one adapter supports the extension, that adapter is used. When multiple adapters claim the same extension (ambiguous format), a generic `BaseAdapter` instance handles loading. When no adapter matches but `BaseAdapter` supports the format, the generic adapter is used as a fallback.

Sources: [data_manager.py](lobster/core/runtime/data_manager.py#L591-L789)

### Modality Loading and Storing

The `load_modality` method orchestrates the full ingestion pipeline: adapter lookup → `from_source` conversion → optional validation → thread-safe storage → provenance logging → IR recording → callback notification. The `store_modality` method is the recommended path for storing *derived* modalities (e.g., clustered data), as it automatically computes lineage metadata, attaches it to `adata.uns['lineage']`, and tracks dirty state for auto-save.

```python
# Loading: explicit adapter selection
adata = dm.load_modality("pbmc", "data/pbmc.h5ad", adapter="transcriptomics_single_cell")

# Storing: automatic lineage tracking
dm.store_modality(
    name="pbmc_clustered",
    adata=adata_clustered,
    parent_name="pbmc",
    step_summary="Clustered into 12 clusters"
)
```

The `store_modality` method supports a `step` parameter that can be any omics-agnostic string — common values include `raw`, `filtered`, `normalized`, `batch_corrected`, `reduced`, `clustered`, `annotated`, `markers`, `de_results`, `pseudobulk`, and `custom`. When a `modality_backend` is attached, ingestion delegates to the backend; otherwise, the modality is marked dirty for deferred auto-save.

### Backed Mode for Large Files

For datasets exceeding 1GB, the DataManager supports **backed-mode loading** where the HDF5 file remains on disk and `.X` is accessed as an HDF5 dataset rather than a full in-memory array. This is controlled by the `backed_mode` constructor parameter or the `LOBSTER_BACKED_MODE=1` environment variable. The `_read_h5ad_smart` function automatically applies backed mode when both the size threshold and the feature flag are met. Callers that need to mutate `.X` must invoke `materialize_modality()` first, which loads the full matrix into memory.

Sources: [data_manager.py](lobster/core/runtime/data_manager.py#L890-L1089), [data_manager.py](lobster/core/runtime/data_manager.py#L165-L214)

## Storage Backends

Backends implement the `IDataBackend` interface, which defines six abstract methods (`load`, `save`, `exists`, `delete`, `list_files`, `get_metadata`) plus optional methods for format detection and path validation. The `BaseBackend` provides shared path resolution, checksum computation, and directory creation logic.

| Backend | Format | Compression | Special Features |
|---|---|---|---|
| **H5ADBackend** | `.h5ad` | gzip (level 6 default) | S3-ready path parsing; `sanitize_anndata` for H5AD compatibility |
| **MuDataBackend** | `.h5mu` | gzip | Multi-modal MuData support; requires `mudata` package |

The `H5ADBackend.sanitize_anndata` method is a critical pre-save step that converts `OrderedDict` → `dict`, tuples → lists, numpy scalars → Python scalars, replaces `/` in keys with `__` (HDF5-safe), and removes columns with `None` names that would cause `PurePosixPath` errors during serialization. This sanitization uses centralized utilities from `lobster.core.utils.h5ad_utils`.

Sources: [backend.py](lobster/core/interfaces/backend.py#L16-L177), [base.py](lobster/core/backends/base.py#L19-L200), [h5ad_backend.py](lobster/core/backends/h5ad_backend.py#L24-L200)

## Thread Safety and Concurrency

The DataManagerV2 is designed for concurrent access from multiple tool calls (e.g., `execute_custom_code` via `asyncio.to_thread`). Two locks protect mutable state: `_session_lock` guards the session file for multi-process safety, and `_state_lock` guards the `modalities` dictionary and dirty set for in-process thread safety. All mutations to `self.modalities` and `self._modality_dirty` are wrapped in `with self._state_lock:` blocks. An LRU eviction mechanism (`_evict_lru_if_needed`) with a configurable cache cap (default 8 modalities) prevents unbounded memory growth in long-running sessions.

> [!TIP]
> The workspace scan uses a 30-second TTL cache (`_scan_ttl`) to avoid redundant filesystem traversal on repeated `get_available_datasets()` calls. This is configurable and balances responsiveness against disk I/O overhead in interactive sessions.

Sources: [data_manager.py](lobster/core/runtime/data_manager.py#L303-L357), [data_manager.py](lobster/core/runtime/data_manager.py#L698-L710)

## Data Flow: End to End

The following diagram traces the complete lifecycle of a dataset from file ingestion through processing to persistence:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as Agent / CLI
    participant DM as DataManagerV2
    participant Reg as Adapter Registry
    participant Adapt as Modality Adapter
    participant Val as Validation
    participant Prov as Provenance Tracker
    participant BE as H5AD Backend

    User->>DM: load_modality(name, source, adapter)
    DM->>Reg: lookup(adapter)
    Reg-->>DM: Adapter instance
    DM->>Adapt: from_source(source, **kwargs)
    Adapt->>Adapt: detect_format → _load_*_data
    Adapt->>Adapt: _create_anndata_from_dataframe
    Adapt->>Adapt: _ensure_numeric_matrix
    Adapt->>Adapt: _add_basic_metadata
    Adapt-->>DM: AnnData object
    DM->>Val: validate(adata, strict=False)
    Val-->>DM: ValidationResult
    DM->>DM: Store in modalities[name]
    DM->>Prov: create_entity + create_data_loading_ir
    DM->>Prov: add_to_anndata(adata)
    DM-->>User: AnnData

    User->>DM: store_modality(name_derived, adata, parent)
    DM->>DM: create_lineage_metadata
    DM->>DM: attach_lineage to adata
    DM->>DM: Mark dirty
    DM->>BE: save (auto or explicit)
    BE->>BE: sanitize_anndata
    BE->>BE: anndata.write_h5ad
```

Sources: [data_manager.py](lobster/core/runtime/data_manager.py#L890-L1089), [adapter.py](lobster/core/interfaces/adapter.py#L29-L48)

## Next Steps

- **[Provenance Tracking and IR](12-provenance-tracking-and-ir)** — Understand how every data transformation is recorded as an intermediate representation for reproducibility and notebook export.

# Provenance Tracking and IR



Lobster implements a **dual-layer provenance architecture** that captures both the *what happened* (activity audit trail) and the *how to reproduce it* (executable intermediate representation) for every data-processing operation. The first layer, managed by `ProvenanceTracker`, records W3C-PROV-aligned activities, entities, and agents with crash-safe disk persistence. The second layer, powered by the **Service-Emitted IR** pattern, embeds `AnalysisStep` objects inside each provenance activity — carrying Jinja2 code templates, typed parameter schemas, and Papermill injection flags that enable deterministic Jupyter notebook generation without manual mapping registries. A complementary `LineageMetadata` system tracks per-modality processing chains directly on AnnData objects via `adata.uns['lineage']`, providing the UI-facing timeline and parent-child derivation graph. Together, these three subsystems ensure that every analytical result produced by Lobster is traceable to its inputs, reproducible via exported notebooks, and auditable across sessions.

## ProvenanceTracker: Activity Audit Trail

The `ProvenanceTracker` is the central provenance recording engine. It models data processing as three first-class concepts drawn from the W3C PROV ontology: **Activities** (operations performed), **Entities** (data artifacts consumed or produced), and **Agents** (software components or persons responsible). Each activity record carries a namespace-scoped identifier (`{namespace}:activity:{uuid}`), an ISO timestamp, input/output entity references, parameters, software version snapshots, and — critically — an optional `ir` field holding a serialized `AnalysisStep`. The tracker is instantiated by `DataManagerV2` and participates in every load, process, and save operation through convenience methods like `log_data_loading`, `log_data_processing`, and `log_data_saving`, which automatically create the surrounding entity and agent records.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "W3C-PROV Model"
        A[Activity] -->|"wasGeneratedBy"| E1[Entity: output]
        E2[Entity: input] -->|"used"| A
        AG[Agent] -->|"wasAssociatedWith"| A
    end

    subgraph "Lobster Implementation"
        PT[ProvenanceTracker] -->|create_activity| A
        PT -->|create_entity| E1
        PT -->|create_entity| E2
        PT -->|create_agent| AG
        A -->|ir field| IR[AnalysisStep]
    end
```

**Disk persistence** follows a JSONL append-only protocol with `fsync` durability guarantees. When a `session_dir` is provided at construction, each `create_activity` call appends a versioned JSON line (`{"v": 1, ...activity}`) to `provenance.jsonl` and updates a companion `metadata.json` with timestamps, activity count, and software versions. On re-initialization — including crash recovery — the tracker loads existing activities line-by-line, skipping corrupt entries with warnings (line-independent recovery). The `provenance_path` property exposes the JSONL file location for external consumers like cloud S3 sync. Provenance data also round-trips through AnnData objects: `add_to_anndata` serializes the full activity/entity/agent graph into `adata.uns['provenance']`, and `extract_from_anndata` restores it, enabling provenance to travel with the data itself. The `get_lineage(entity_id)` method performs recursive backward tracing from any entity through its producing activities and their input entities, reconstructing the complete derivation chain.

Sources: [provenance.py](lobster/core/provenance/provenance.py#L1-L100), [provenance.py](lobster/core/provenance/provenance.py#L200-L400), [provenance.py](lobster/core/provenance/provenance.py#L400-L600), [provenance.py](lobster/core/provenance/provenance.py#L600-L714)

## AnalysisStep: Service-Emitted Intermediate Representation

The `AnalysisStep` dataclass is the **single source of truth** for how a service operation should be represented in an exported notebook. Rather than maintaining a central registry that maps tool names to code templates (a coupling nightmare), Lobster inverts the dependency: each service *emits* an `AnalysisStep` alongside its result, encapsulating everything needed for deterministic code generation. This design means that adding a new analysis operation requires zero changes to the notebook export pipeline — the service itself defines its reproducible representation.

| Field | Purpose | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `operation` | Fully-qualified operation name | `"scanpy.tl.leiden"` |
| `tool_name` | Original tool name for provenance linking | `"cluster_and_visualize"` |
| `library` | Required library | `"scanpy"` |
| `code_template` | Jinja2 template with `{{ variable }}` placeholders | `"sc.tl.leiden(adata, resolution={{ resolution }})"` |
| `imports` | Import statements for notebook cell | `["import scanpy as sc"]` |
| `parameters` | Actual parameter values from this execution | `{"resolution": 1.0}` |
| `parameter_schema` | Typed specs with Papermill flags per parameter | `{"resolution": ParameterSpec(...)}` |
| `input_entities` / `output_entities` | Data flow references | `["adata"]` / `["adata"]` |
| `execution_context` | Seeds, versions, timestamps | `{"algorithm": "leiden"}` |
| `validates_on_export` | Run AST validation on export | `True` |
| `requires_validation` | Full execution validation recommended | `False` |
| `exportable` | Include in notebook export | `True` |
| `helper_code` | Shared functions injected into notebook helper cell | `["def plot_clusters(...):"]` |

The `ParameterSpec` dataclass provides the type-level contract for each parameter: `param_type` (Python type as string), `papermill_injectable` (whether Papermill can override it at notebook execution time), `default_value`, `required` flag, optional `validation_rule` expression, and `description`. During serialization, `ParameterSpec.to_dict()` enforces JSON-serializability of `default_value` with an explicit `TypeError` on failure — catching non-serializable defaults at IR creation time rather than at export time. Deserialization in `AnalysisStep.from_dict()` reconstructs `ParameterSpec` objects from dictionaries, gracefully handling legacy JSON Schema-style dicts (with `"type"` instead of `"param_type"`) by passing them through unchanged.

The **render pipeline** works in three stages: `validate_template()` parses the Jinja2 template for syntactic correctness; `render(**override_params)` merges override parameters with stored values and produces a Python code string; `validate_rendered_code()` runs `ast.parse()` on the result to verify syntactic validity before any notebook cell is written. The `get_papermill_parameters()` method extracts only the `papermill_injectable=True` parameters, producing the dictionary that populates the notebook's tagged parameters cell for parameterized execution.

Sources: [analysis_ir.py](lobster/core/provenance/analysis_ir.py#L1-L200), [analysis_ir.py](lobster/core/provenance/analysis_ir.py#L200-L400), [analysis_ir.py](lobster/core/provenance/analysis_ir.py#L400-L623)

## The 3-Tuple Return Contract

Services integrate with the provenance system through a consistent **3-tuple return pattern**: every IR-emitting method returns `(result_data, statistics_dict, AnalysisStep)`. The `ClusteringService` demonstrates this pattern concretely — its `run_pca` method, for example, returns `(AnnData, stats_dict, AnalysisStep)`, where the `AnalysisStep` carries a full Jinja2 template for the PCA pipeline (including scaling, feature subsetting, and the PCA call itself), typed parameter schemas for `n_comps`, `scale_data`, and `use_highly_variable`, and an `execution_context` recording the operation type and algorithm details.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant DM as DataManagerV2
    participant S as Service (e.g. ClusteringService)
    participant PT as ProvenanceTracker
    participant IR as AnalysisStep

    DM->>S: run_pca(adata, n_comps=30)
    S->>S: Execute analysis
    S->>IR: _create_clustering_ir(params)
    Note over IR: Build Jinja2 template<br/>+ ParameterSpec schemas
    S-->>DM: (adata, stats, AnalysisStep)
    DM->>PT: create_activity(type="pca", ir=AnalysisStep)
    PT->>PT: Serialize IR → dict
    PT->>PT: Append to provenance.jsonl
    PT-->>DM: activity_id
```

The `ClusteringService._create_clustering_ir` method is particularly instructive because it demonstrates **conditional template generation**: when `feature_selection_method == "deviance"`, the Jinja2 template includes deviance-based feature selection (operating on raw counts before normalization), while the `"hvg"` path uses Seurat-style highly variable gene selection (operating on normalized data). Both paths produce complete end-to-end pipeline templates — feature selection through normalization, scaling, PCA, neighbors, clustering, and UMAP — ensuring that the exported notebook reproduces the full analysis rather than isolated steps. This is the key architectural insight: the IR captures *pipeline-level* semantics, not just individual function calls.

Sources: [clustering_service.py](lobster/services/analysis/clustering_service.py#L1-L200), [clustering_service.py](lobster/services/analysis/clustering_service.py#L200-L400)

## LineageMetadata: Per-Modality Processing Chains

While `ProvenanceTracker` operates at the session level (tracking all activities across all modalities), `LineageMetadata` operates at the **individual AnnData level**, embedded directly in `adata.uns['lineage']`. This dual-layer design separates the global audit trail from the local derivation graph, enabling the UI to display per-modality timelines without querying the full provenance store.

The lineage schema contains six fields: `base_name` (original dataset name stripped of processing suffixes), `version` (sequential integer, 1 = raw), `processing_step` (canonical step name like `"filtered_normalized"` or any domain-specific string), `parent_modality` (name of the modality this was derived from, `None` for raw), `step_summary` (human-readable change description), and `created_at` (ISO timestamp). The `CANONICAL_STEPS` set defines standard steps (`raw`, `quality_assessed`, `filtered`, `normalized`, `batch_corrected`, `reduced`, `clustered`, `subclustered`, `annotated`, `markers`, `de_results`, `pseudobulk`, `custom`), but any string is valid — agent packages can define domain-specific steps like `"imputed"` or `"peak_called"` without modifying core.

**Suffix-based inference** provides automatic lineage metadata creation from modality naming conventions. The `extract_base_name` function iteratively strips known suffixes (sorted longest-first for correct matching) from modality names: `geo_gse12345_filtered_normalized_clustered` resolves to base name `geo_gse12345` by stripping `_clustered`, then `_filtered_normalized`. The `infer_processing_step` function maps the outermost suffix to its canonical step string. The `create_lineage_metadata` factory function auto-computes all fields: `base_name` from the modality name or inherited from a parent AnnData, `version` incremented from the parent's version, and `step` inferred from the suffix. For backward compatibility with legacy h5ad files lacking lineage metadata, `ensure_lineage` creates synthetic lineage with a `_synthetic` flag.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["geo_gse12345<br/>v=1, step=raw"] --> B["geo_gse12345_filtered<br/>v=2, step=filtered"]
    B --> C["geo_gse12345_filtered_normalized<br/>v=3, step=filtered_normalized"]
    C --> D["geo_gse12345_filtered_normalized_clustered<br/>v=4, step=clustered"]
    C --> E["geo_gse12345_filtered_normalized_batch_corrected<br/>v=4, step=batch_corrected"]
    D --> F["geo_gse12345_filtered_normalized_clustered_annotated<br/>v=5, step=annotated"]
```

Sources: [lineage.py](lobster/core/provenance/lineage.py#L1-L200), [lineage.py](lobster/core/provenance/lineage.py#L200-L324)

## IR Coverage Analysis

The `IRCoverageAnalyzer` provides **static analysis** of IR adoption across the service layer, answering the operational question: *which services emit IR and which methods are still uncovered?* It parses service files using Python's `ast` module, detecting `AnalysisStep` imports and identifying IR-emitting methods by their return pattern — specifically, functions that return a 3-element tuple where the third element's variable name contains `"ir"`, `"step"`, or `"analysis"`. This heuristic matches the standard `(result, stats, AnalysisStep)` convention.

The analyzer produces a `CoverageReport` containing per-service `ServiceCoverage` objects (with `has_ir_import`, `methods_with_ir`, `methods_without_ir`, and `coverage_percentage`) and aggregate statistics (total services, services with IR, overall coverage percentage). The `identify_gaps` method returns a list of `(service_name, method_name)` tuples for all uncovered methods, enabling targeted IR implementation. A CLI entry point (`python -m lobster.core.provenance.ir_coverage`) supports `--services-dir`, `--pattern`, `--verbose`, `--json`, and `--gaps-only` flags, exiting with code 1 if overall coverage falls below the 60% target threshold. This CI-integrable check prevents regression in IR coverage as new services are added.

> [!TIP]
> When adding a new service method, return the 3-tuple `(result, stats, AnalysisStep)` pattern so the `IRCoverageAnalyzer` AST heuristic detects it automatically. Use `create_minimal_ir()` as a scaffolding fallback for methods where full IR isn't yet available — the generated notebook will include a TODO marker, and the method will still count as IR-covered.

Sources: [ir_coverage.py](lobster/core/provenance/ir_coverage.py#L1-L200), [ir_coverage.py](lobster/core/provenance/ir_coverage.py#L200-L473)

## IR Factory Functions and Notebook Integration

The `analysis_ir` module provides factory functions for common I/O operations that every notebook needs: `create_data_loading_ir` generates an `AnalysisStep` for `anndata.read_h5ad` with a Papermill-injectable file path parameter, and `create_data_saving_ir` generates one for `adata.write_h5ad` with configurable compression and output prefix. These are imported and used directly by `DataManagerV2` during load and save operations, ensuring that even the bookend operations of a notebook (read data in, write results out) carry full IR.

The `create_minimal_ir` function serves as the **scaffolding fallback** for operations that haven't received full IR treatment yet. It produces an `AnalysisStep` with `validates_on_export=False` and `requires_validation=True`, embedding a TODO comment in the code template. This allows the notebook export pipeline to function without gaps while signaling that manual review is needed. The `validate_ir_list` utility validates a batch of IR dictionaries — checking deserialization, template syntax, and required field completeness — returning a list of error messages for any issues. The `extract_unique_imports` function deduplicates and sorts imports across multiple IR objects using the stdlib → third-party → local convention, and `extract_unique_helper_code` preserves insertion order while deduplicating helper code blocks.

> [!TIP]
> The `AnalysisStep.render()` method accepts `**override_params` that merge with stored parameters, enabling Papermill to inject runtime values into the Jinja2 template. For parameters that should always be injectable (like file paths and resolution values), mark them `papermill_injectable=True` in the `ParameterSpec` — the notebook exporter uses `get_papermill_parameters()` to populate the tagged parameters cell automatically.

Sources: [analysis_ir.py](lobster/core/provenance/analysis_ir.py#L399-L623), [data_manager.py](lobster/core/runtime/data_manager.py#L1-L80)

## Identifier Provenance: Dataset Ownership Validation

Beyond computational provenance, Lobster implements **identifier provenance** through the `IdentifierProvenanceService` — a specialized service that validates whether a dataset identifier belongs to the study being analyzed or to a referenced study. This addresses a critical correctness issue: extracted identifiers from referenced studies were previously treated identically to the study's own data, leading to wrong datasets being queued for download.

The service implements a two-layer validation system. **Layer 1** (section-based extraction) distinguishes identifiers found in a publication's Data Availability section (marked `"primary"`, confidence 0.95) from those found only in Methods or Body text (marked `"uncertain"`, confidence 0.3). **Layer 2** (E-Link validation) uses NCBI's Entrez link API to verify whether a BioProject identifier links back to the source publication's PMID — if validated, uncertain identifiers are upgraded to `"referenced"` with a confidence boost. The `is_downloadable` flag applies strict logic: only `access_type == "open"` AND `provenance == "primary"` identifiers are auto-queued for download, preventing controlled-access or uncertain-provenance datasets from entering the pipeline without explicit user consent.

Sources: [identifier_provenance_service.py](lobster/services/metadata/identifier_provenance_service.py#L1-L200)

## Architecture Summary

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Session-Level Provenance"
        PT[ProvenanceTracker] -->|JSONL persistence| PF[provenance.jsonl]
        PT -->|metadata| MF[metadata.json]
        PT -->|activities contain| IR[AnalysisStep IR]
    end

    subgraph "Modality-Level Lineage"
        LM[LineageMetadata] -->|embedded in| AD["adata.uns<br/>'lineage'"]
        AD -->|base_name + version| UI[UI Timeline Display]
        AD -->|parent_modality| LG[Derivation Graph]
    end

    subgraph "Service Layer"
        CS[ClusteringService] -->|"3-tuple return"| DM[DataManagerV2]
        PS[PathwayEnrichmentService] -->|"3-tuple return"| DM
        DM -->|create_activity| PT
        DM -->|attach_lineage| AD
    end

    subgraph "Notebook Export"
        IR -->|render + validate| NB[Jupyter Notebook]
        IR -->|get_papermill_parameters| PC[Parameters Cell]
        IRCA[IRCoverageAnalyzer] -->|AST scan| CS
        IRCA -->|AST scan| PS
    end

    subgraph "Identifier Provenance"
        IPS[IdentifierProvenanceService] -->|section-based| PRI[Primary vs Referenced]
        IPS -->|E-Link validation| ELI[NCBI Entrez Links]
    end
```

The three provenance subsystems address distinct concerns at different granularity levels. `ProvenanceTracker` provides the **global audit trail** — who did what, when, with what software, connected to what inputs and outputs. `AnalysisStep` IR provides the **reproducibility contract** — exact code templates, typed parameters, and validation flags that enable deterministic notebook generation. `LineageMetadata` provides the **per-modality derivation graph** — version chains and processing steps that enable UI timeline display and parent-child navigation. The `IdentifierProvenanceService` adds a fourth dimension: **dataset ownership validation** that prevents incorrect data from entering the pipeline. Together, they ensure that every result in Lobster is traceable, reproducible, and correct.

Sources: [provenance.py](lobster/core/provenance/provenance.py#L1-L100), [analysis_ir.py](lobster/core/provenance/analysis_ir.py#L1-L100), [lineage.py](lobster/core/provenance/lineage.py#L1-L100), [ir_coverage.py](lobster/core/provenance/ir_coverage.py#L1-L100), [identifier_provenance_service.py](lobster/services/metadata/identifier_provenance_service.py#L1-L100)
