# Notebook Export Pipeline



Lobster's Notebook Export Pipeline transforms live analysis sessions into **executable, reproducible Jupyter notebooks** through a Service-Emitted Intermediate Representation (IR) architecture. Rather than relying on brittle manual mapping registries that translate tool calls into code, each service emits structured `AnalysisStep` IR objects containing Jinja2 code templates, import declarations, and parameter schemas — enabling **deterministic, 95%+ executable notebook generation** from provenance records alone. The pipeline spans four stages: provenance capture during analysis, IR-driven code generation during export, multi-level validation, and Papermill-parameterized replay execution.

Sources: [exporter.py](lobster/core/notebooks/exporter.py#L1-L9), [analysis_ir.py](lobster/core/provenance/analysis_ir.py#L1-L8)

## Architectural Overview

The pipeline's central insight is that **provenance and code generation are unified through IR**. When a service performs an operation (e.g., `scanpy.pp.normalize_total`), it records not just *what happened* in the provenance log, but *how to reproduce it* via an embedded `AnalysisStep` object. The exporter then separates exportable analysis steps from provenance-only orchestration activities, rendering each IR into a notebook cell.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Session["Live Analysis Session"]
        S1[Service Operation] -->|emits| IR[AnalysisStep IR]
        IR -->|embedded in| PT[ProvenanceTracker]
        PT -->|persists to| JSONL["provenance.jsonl"]
    end

    subgraph Export["Notebook Export"]
        PT -->|activities + IR| NE[NotebookExporter]
        NE -->|filter| EIR["Exportable IR Pairs"]
        EIR -->|Jinja2 render| NB["Jupyter Notebook .ipynb"]
    end

    subgraph Validation["Pre-Execution Validation"]
        NB -->|syntax + imports| NV[NotebookValidator]
        NV -->|results| VR[NotebookValidationResult]
    end

    subgraph Replay["Pipeline Replay"]
        NB -->|parameterize| PM[Papermill Executor]
        PM -->|inject params| OUT["Executed Notebook"]
    end

    style IR fill:#4a9eff,color:#fff
    style EIR fill:#4a9eff,color:#fff
    style NB fill:#2ecc71,color:#fff
```

Sources: [exporter.py](lobster/core/notebooks/exporter.py#L66-L206), [provenance.py](lobster/core/provenance/provenance.py#L33-L79)

## The AnalysisStep IR: Single Source of Truth

The `AnalysisStep` dataclass is the **canonical contract** between services and the notebook export pipeline. Every field serves a precise purpose in code generation — nothing is decorative.

| Field | Purpose | Example |
|-------|---------|---------|
| `operation` | Fully-qualified operation name | `"scanpy.pp.normalize_total"` |
| `code_template` | Jinja2 template with `{{ variable }}` placeholders | `"sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum={{ target }})"` |
| `imports` | Required import statements | `["import scanpy as sc"]` |
| `parameters` | Actual parameter values from execution | `{"target": 1e4}` |
| `parameter_schema` | `ParameterSpec` entries with Papermill flags | `{"target": ParameterSpec(...)}` |
| `helper_code` | Shared functions injected into helper cell | `["def _filter_cells(adata, min_genes): ..."]` |
| `exportable` | Whether to include in notebook export | `True` (default) or `False` for orchestration |
| `validates_on_export` | Run AST validation on export | `True` (default) |

> [!TIP]
> The `exportable` field is the **critical filter gate** — services that perform orchestration (publication processing, metadata extraction) set `exportable=False` so their activities remain in the provenance audit trail but are excluded from the executable notebook. This prevents non-reproducible orchestration steps from breaking pipeline replay.

Sources: [analysis_ir.py](lobster/core/provenance/analysis_ir.py#L104-L183)

### ParameterSpec and Papermill Integration

Each parameter within `parameter_schema` carries a `ParameterSpec` that declares its type, injectability, and validation rules. Parameters marked `papermill_injectable=True` are extracted into a dedicated **Papermill-tagged parameters cell**, enabling downstream users to override values via the command line without editing the notebook:

```bash
papermill notebook.ipynb output.ipynb \
    -p input_data "new_dataset.h5ad" \
    -p min_genes 200
```

The `get_papermill_parameters()` method on `AnalysisStep` collects all injectable parameters, and the exporter merges them into the parameters cell while deduplicating against standard parameters (`input_data`, `output_prefix`, `random_seed`).

Sources: [analysis_ir.py](lobster/core/provenance/analysis_ir.py#L19-L101), [analysis_ir.py](lobster/core/provenance/analysis_ir.py#L321-L336), [exporter.py](lobster/core/notebooks/exporter.py#L565-L622)

## Export Pipeline: From Provenance to Notebook

### Activity Filtering

The `NotebookExporter.export()` method begins by filtering provenance activities based on a `filter_strategy`:

| Strategy | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| `"successful"` | Exclude activities with `error` markers or `type="failed_operation"` |
| `"all"` | Include every recorded activity |
| `"manual"` | Falls back to `"successful"` (not yet implemented) |

After filtering, `_get_exportable_activity_ir_pairs()` further separates activities into two categories: **exportable pairs** (activity + `AnalysisStep` where `exportable=True`) and **provenance-only activities** (no IR, or `exportable=False`). This two-tier filtering ensures notebooks contain only executable code while the complete audit trail remains in provenance.

Sources: [exporter.py](lobster/core/notebooks/exporter.py#L208-L230), [exporter.py](lobster/core/notebooks/exporter.py#L271-L320)

### Notebook Cell Generation Order

The exporter assembles cells in a precise sequence designed for top-to-bottom execution:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    H[Header<br/>Markdown] --> IM[Integrity Manifest<br/>Markdown]
    IM --> I[Imports<br/>Code]
    I --> HC[Helper Functions<br/>Code]
    HC --> P[Parameters<br/>Code + Papermill Tag]
    P --> DL[Data Loading<br/>Code]
    DL --> S1["Step N: Doc<br/>Markdown"]
    S1 --> S2["Step N: Code<br/>Code"]
    S2 --> DS[Data Saving<br/>Code]
    DS --> PS[Provenance Summary<br/>Markdown]
    PS --> F[Footer<br/>Markdown]

    style P fill:#e67e22,color:#fff
    style DL fill:#2ecc71,color:#fff
    style DS fill:#2ecc71,color:#fff
```

| Cell | Source | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| Header | `_create_header_cell()` | Session stats, IR coverage percentage, Lobster version |
| Integrity Manifest | `_create_integrity_manifest_cell()` | SHA-256 hashes for ALCOA+ / 21 CFR Part 11 compliance |
| Imports | `_create_imports_cell()` | Deduplicated via `extract_unique_imports()` — sorted stdlib → third-party → local |
| Helper Functions | `_create_helper_code_cell()` | Shared functions from `ir.helper_code`, deduplicated by exact match |
| Parameters | `_create_parameters_cell()` | Tagged `"parameters"` for Papermill; merges IR-derived + standard params |
| Data Loading | `_create_data_loading_cell()` | Skipped if download activity provides its own load code |
| Analysis Steps | `_ir_to_code_cell()` | One doc + one code cell per exportable IR; `load_dataset`/`save_dataset` types skipped |
| Data Saving | `_create_data_saving_cell()` | Renders `save_dataset` IR if present, otherwise fallback H5AD write |
| Provenance Summary | `_create_provenance_summary_cell()` | Table of executable vs. provenance-only activity counts |
| Footer | `_create_footer_cell()` | Papermill usage instructions, IR coverage explanation |

> [!TIP]
> The **data loading cell is conditionally omitted** when a download activity (e.g., `geo_service.download_dataset`, `sra_download`, `pride.download.download_dataset`, `metabolights.download.download_dataset`) is present in the exportable IR pairs. Download IRs produce their own data-loading code, so the generic `ad.read_h5ad(input_data)` cell would fail by referencing a non-existent `input_data` parameter.

Sources: [exporter.py](lobster/core/notebooks/exporter.py#L124-L206), [exporter.py](lobster/core/notebooks/exporter.py#L322-L344), [exporter.py](lobster/core/notebooks/exporter.py#L513-L563)

### Code Rendering from IR Templates

Each `AnalysisStep.code_template` is a **Jinja2 template** rendered with the step's `parameters` dictionary. The `render()` method merges parameters with optional overrides and returns executable Python:

```python
# Template: "sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum={{ target }})"
# Parameters: {"target": 1e4}
# Rendered:   "sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=10000.0)"
```

When `validates_on_export=True`, the rendered code is run through `ast.parse()` to catch syntax errors before writing the notebook. Failures are annotated inline rather than causing export abort — the problematic code is preserved with a `# SYNTAX ERROR` comment prefix for manual review.

Sources: [analysis_ir.py](lobster/core/provenance/analysis_ir.py#L270-L319), [exporter.py](lobster/core/notebooks/exporter.py#L806-L848)

### Data Integrity and Compliance

The integrity manifest cell records **SHA-256 cryptographic hashes** of all input data files, provenance records, and system state. This satisfies ALCOA+ (Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate) principles and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic record requirements:

- **Provenance hash**: SHA-256 of serialized `namespace`, `activities_count`, `entities_count`
- **Input file hashes**: SHA-256 of each modality's `.h5ad` file (chunked 4096-byte reads for memory efficiency)
- **System info**: Lobster version, Python version, platform, Git commit hash (8-char short)

Sources: [exporter.py](lobster/core/notebooks/exporter.py#L394-L511)

## Validation Layer

The `NotebookValidator` provides **two validation modes** that run before notebook execution:

| Mode | Method | Scope |
|------|--------|-------|
| Full | `validate()` | Syntax + import resolution + anti-pattern detection |
| Quick | `validate_quick()` | AST syntax check only, no import resolution |

Full validation produces a `NotebookValidationResult` containing:

- **Syntax errors**: Caught via `ast.parse()` on each code cell, reported with cell index and line number
- **Import resolution**: Each discovered import checked via `importlib.util.find_spec()` — unresolved imports are errors (strict mode) or warnings (lenient mode)
- **Anti-patterns**: Detected via heuristic checks — `exec()`/`eval()` usage, bare `except:` clauses, excessive `print()` statements (>5 per cell)

Sources: [validator.py](lobster/core/notebooks/validator.py#L151-L236), [validator.py](lobster/core/notebooks/validator.py#L341-L394), [validator.py](lobster/core/notebooks/validator.py#L396-L421)

## Execution and Replay

The `NotebookExecutor` wraps Papermill for **parameterized notebook execution**, enabling the classic "export once, replay on new data" workflow.

### Execution Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START[Execute Request] --> V[Validate Input]
    V -->|errors| FAIL["status: validation_failed"]
    V -->|pass| PREP[Prepare Parameters]
    PREP --> PM[Papermill execute_notebook]
    PM -->|success| OK["status: success<br/>execution_time recorded"]
    PM -->|exception| ERR["status: failed<br/>error_type + failed_cell"]

    style FAIL fill:#e74c3c,color:#fff
    style OK fill:#2ecc71,color:#fff
    style ERR fill:#e74c3c,color:#fff
```

### Input Validation Before Execution

Before running Papermill, `validate_input()` checks compatibility between the input H5AD file and notebook metadata expectations:

| Check | Severity | Logic |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Cell count | Warning | `adata.n_obs < metadata.min_cells` (default 100) |
| Required columns | Error | Missing columns from `metadata.required_obs_columns` |
| Sparse data | Warning | Input is sparse when dense may be expected |

### Dry-Run Simulation

The `dry_run()` method provides a **no-execution preview** — it runs input validation, counts code cells, and estimates execution time at ~2 minutes per cell. This allows users to assess feasibility before committing compute resources.

### Parameter Discovery

`list_parameters()` extracts the Papermill-tagged parameters cell and parses variable assignments, returning a dictionary of parameter names and default values. This enables programmatic discovery of what a notebook expects without manual inspection.

Sources: [executor.py](lobster/core/notebooks/executor.py#L70-L268), [executor.py](lobster/core/notebooks/executor.py#L150-L187), [executor.py](lobster/core/notebooks/executor.py#L329-L366)

## IR Factory Functions

The `analysis_ir` module provides factory functions for common operations that don't originate from a specific service:

| Factory | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `create_data_loading_ir()` | Generates IR for `anndata.read_h5ad()` with Papermill-injectable `input_data` parameter |
| `create_data_saving_ir()` | Generates IR for `adata.write_h5ad()` with configurable compression |
| `create_minimal_ir()` | Fallback for services without full IR support — produces `TODO`-marked cells |

The `create_minimal_ir()` function is the **onboarding pathway** for new services: it creates an `AnalysisStep` with `validates_on_export=False` and `requires_validation=True`, ensuring the exported notebook flags the cell for manual review while still recording the operation in provenance. Services can then upgrade to full IR support by implementing proper `code_template` and `parameter_schema` values.

Sources: [analysis_ir.py](lobster/core/provenance/analysis_ir.py#L464-L496), [analysis_ir.py](lobster/core/provenance/analysis_ir.py#L499-L552), [analysis_ir.py](lobster/core/provenance/analysis_ir.py#L555-L598)

## Provenance Persistence and IR Recovery

The `ProvenanceTracker` supports **disk persistence** via a `session_dir` parameter, writing activities to `provenance.jsonl` with crash-safe `fsync` semantics. Each line is a self-contained JSON record with schema version `v:1`, enabling line-independent recovery — corrupt lines are skipped, and the remaining activities load successfully.

When loading from disk, the tracker reconstructs `AnalysisStep` objects from serialized IR dictionaries:

```python
# During _load_from_disk():
if data.get("ir") is not None:
    data["ir"] = AnalysisStep.from_dict(data["ir"])
```

This means the **round-trip is complete**: services emit IR → provenance persists to disk → notebook exporter reads from restored provenance → IR renders to executable code. Cross-session notebook export is fully supported.

Sources: [provenance.py](lobster/core/provenance/provenance.py#L41-L79), [provenance.py](lobster/core/provenance/provenance.py#L80-L122), [provenance.py](lobster/core/provenance/provenance.py#L124-L150)

## Module Organization

The notebook pipeline lives under `lobster/core/notebooks/` with backward-compatible shims at the legacy paths:

| Module | Path | Legacy Shim |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `NotebookExporter` | `lobster.core.notebooks.exporter` | `lobster.core.notebook_exporter` (deprecated, removed v2.0.0) |
| `NotebookValidator` | `lobster.core.notebooks.validator` | `lobster.core.notebook_validator` (deprecated) |
| `NotebookExecutor` | `lobster.core.notebooks.executor` | `lobster.core.notebook_executor` (deprecated) |
| `AnalysisStep` IR | `lobster.core.provenance.analysis_ir` | — |
| `ProvenanceTracker` | `lobster.core.provenance.provenance` | — |

Sources: [notebook_exporter.py](lobster/core/notebook_exporter.py#L1-L12), [notebooks/__init__.py](lobster/core/notebooks/__init__.py#L1)

---

**Next**: Understand how provenance records are constructed before they reach the export pipeline in [Provenance Tracking and IR](12-provenance-tracking-and-ir), or see how domain services emit IR objects in [Transcriptomics and Genomics Agents](14-transcriptomics-and-genomics-agents).

# Transcriptomics and Genomics Agents



The Transcriptomics and Genomics domain packages implement Lobster's multi-agent analysis capabilities for RNA-seq and genomic variation data. Together, `lobster-transcriptomics` and `lobster-genomics` form a hierarchical agent architecture where parent orchestrators handle workflow routing and core analysis, while specialized sub-agents execute focused tasks like cell type annotation, differential expression, and clinical variant interpretation. Each agent registers itself via `AGENT_CONFIG` entry points, enabling the [Supervisor Agent](5-supervisor-agent-and-routing) to discover and hand off tasks automatically through the [Agent Registry](7-agent-registry-and-discovery).

Sources: [transcriptomics_expert.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/agents/transcriptomics/transcriptomics_expert.py#L1-L45), [genomics_expert.py](packages/lobster-genomics/lobster/agents/genomics/genomics_expert.py#L1-L40), [pyproject.toml](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/pyproject.toml#L58-L63), [pyproject.toml](packages/lobster-genomics/pyproject.toml#L42-L43)

## Architectural Overview

The two packages share an identical structural pattern — a **parent-child agent hierarchy** orchestrated through LangGraph `create_react_agent` factory functions. Parent agents hold direct tool access for high-frequency operations (QC, loading, clustering) and delegate to child agents via `handoff_to_*` delegation tools. Children are **not supervisor-accessible** (`supervisor_accessible=False`), enforcing a strict delegation chain: Supervisor → Parent → Child.

```mermaid
graph TD
    SUP["Supervisor Agent"] -->|handoff_to_transcriptomics_expert| TE["Transcriptomics Expert<br/>(Parent)"]
    SUP -->|handoff_to_genomics_expert| GE["Genomics Expert<br/>(Parent)"]

    TE -->|handoff_to_annotation_expert| AE["Annotation Expert<br/>(Child)"]
    TE -->|handoff_to_de_analysis_expert| DE["DE Analysis Expert<br/>(Child)"]

    GE -->|handoff_to_variant_analysis_expert| VA["Variant Analysis Expert<br/>(Child)"]

    subgraph "lobster-transcriptomics"
        TE
        AE
        DE
    end

    subgraph "lobster-genomics"
        GE
        VA
    end

    style SUP fill:#4a90d9,color:#fff
    style TE fill:#2d8659,color:#fff
    style GE fill:#8b5cf6,color:#fff
    style AE fill:#5cb85c,color:#fff
    style DE fill:#5cb85c,color:#fff
    style VA fill:#a78bfa,color:#fff
```

Each agent is built by a factory function that initializes LLM configuration, instantiates stateless services, creates closure-scoped `@tool` functions with access to `DataManagerV2`, and returns a configured `ReAct agent`. The factory pattern ensures tools are bound to the correct `data_manager` instance at creation time, avoiding shared mutable state between agent instances.

Sources: [transcriptomics_expert.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/agents/transcriptomics/transcriptomics_expert.py#L48-L120), [genomics_expert.py](packages/lobster-genomics/lobster/agents/genomics/genomics_expert.py#L28-L39), [annotation_expert.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/agents/transcriptomics/annotation_expert.py#L29-L37), [variant_analysis_expert.py](packages/lobster-genomics/lobster/agents/genomics/variant_analysis_expert.py#L20-L28)

## Agent Registry and Entry Points

Both packages declare agents through Python entry points in `pyproject.toml` under the `lobster.agents` namespace. At runtime, each agent module exposes an `AGENT_CONFIG` instance of `AgentRegistryConfig` at module level, which the registry reads to discover agent metadata, factory functions, handoff tool names, and child agent relationships.

| Package | Entry Point | `supervisor_accessible` | Child Agents |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lobster-transcriptomics` | `transcriptomics_expert` | `true` | `annotation_expert`, `de_analysis_expert` |
| `lobster-transcriptomics` | `annotation_expert` | `false` | — |
| `lobster-transcriptomics` | `de_analysis_expert` | `false` | — |
| `lobster-genomics` | `genomics_expert` | `true` | `variant_analysis_expert` |
| `lobster-genomics` | `variant_analysis_expert` | `false` | — |

The transcriptomics package also registers state classes under the `lobster.states` entry point namespace, enabling the graph topology to reconstruct typed state during agent handoffs.

> [!TIP]
> When `supervisor_accessible=False`, the agent has no `handoff_tool_name` — the supervisor cannot route tasks to it directly. This is intentional: annotation and DE analysis require context (QC results, cluster assignments) that only the parent agent possesses. Bypassing the parent would lead to missing-modality or missing-column errors.

Sources: [pyproject.toml](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/pyproject.toml#L58-L68), [pyproject.toml](packages/lobster-genomics/pyproject.toml#L42-L43), [annotation_expert.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/agents/transcriptomics/annotation_expert.py#L29-L37), [de_analysis_expert.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/agents/transcriptomics/de_analysis_expert.py#L23-L31)

## Transcriptomics Expert — Parent Orchestrator

The **Transcriptomics Expert** is a unified parent agent handling both single-cell and bulk RNA-seq workflows. Its defining capability is **automatic data type detection**: when a modality is accessed, the `detect_data_type()` function applies three heuristics in priority order — observation count (>500 suggests single-cell, <100 suggests bulk), presence of single-cell-specific `obs` columns (`n_counts`, `leiden`, `louvain`), and matrix sparsity (>70% sparse suggests single-cell). This classification drives which QC defaults are applied and which workflow the agent follows.

### Auto-Detection Heuristics and QC Defaults

The `detect_data_type()` function returns `Literal["single_cell", "bulk"]`, and `get_qc_defaults()` maps that result to parameter presets:

| Parameter | Single-Cell Default | Bulk Default | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| `min_genes` | 200 | 1000 | Scanpy standard vs. higher bulk threshold |
| `max_genes` | 5000 | None | Doublet filtering for SC; not applicable for bulk |
| `min_cells_per_gene` | 3 | 2 | Standard rare-gene filter for each modality |
| `max_mt_pct` | 20.0 | 30.0 | Dying cell cutoff; more permissive for bulk |
| `target_sum` | 10000 | 1000000 | CPM for SC; TPM/CPM for bulk |
| `normalization_method` | `log1p` | `log1p` | Standard Scanpy normalization for both |

> [!TIP]
> For cardiac/muscle tissue or metabolically active cells (neurons, hepatocytes), override `max_mt_pct` to 30–50% — these cells naturally have higher mitochondrial content. For proliferative populations, relax `max_genes` to 8000–10000 to avoid filtering legitimate high-complexity cells.

### Shared Tools and Direct Tools

The parent agent assembles its tool set from two sources: **shared tools** (created by `create_shared_tools()`) and **direct tools** (defined inline in the factory function). Shared tools auto-detect data type and work for both SC and bulk, while direct tools are modality-specific.

| Tool | Source | AQUADIF Category | SC | Bulk | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `check_data_status` | Shared | UTILITY | ✓ | ✓ | List modalities, detect type, report dimensions |
| `assess_data_quality` | Shared | QUALITY | ✓ | ✓ | QC metrics with auto-defaults |
| `filter_and_normalize` | Shared | PREPROCESS | ✓ | ✓ | Filter + normalize with auto-defaults |
| `select_variable_features` | Shared | PREPROCESS | ✓ | ✓ | HVG or deviance feature selection |
| `run_pca` | Shared | ANALYZE | ✓ | ✓ | PCA reduction |
| `compute_neighbors_and_embed` | Shared | ANALYZE | ✓ | ✓ | KNN graph + UMAP |
| `cluster_cells` | Direct | ANALYZE | ✓ | ✗ | Full clustering pipeline (Leiden/Louvain) |
| `subcluster_cells` | Direct | ANALYZE | ✓ | ✗ | Re-cluster specific clusters |
| `find_marker_genes` | Direct | ANALYZE | ✓ | ✓ | Rank genes per group |
| `import_bulk_counts` | Direct | IMPORT | ✗ | ✓ | Load from Salmon/kallisto/featureCounts/CSV |
| `merge_sample_metadata` | Direct | IMPORT | ✗ | ✓ | Join sample metadata |
| `assess_bulk_sample_quality` | Direct | QUALITY | ✗ | ✓ | Outlier detection for bulk |
| `filter_bulk_genes` | Direct | PREPROCESS | ✗ | ✓ | Remove low-expression genes |
| `normalize_bulk_counts` | Direct | PREPROCESS | ✗ | ✓ | DESeq2 VST or log1p |
| `detect_batch_effects` | Direct | ANALYZE | ✓ | ✓ | Batch detection |
| `integrate_batches` | Direct | ANALYZE | ✓ | ✓ | Harmony integration |

### Delegation Protocol

The transcriptomics expert enforces **mandatory immediate delegation** — when the agent identifies annotation or DE tasks, it must invoke the delegation tool in its next action rather than describing or suggesting it. This is codified in the system prompt with explicit trigger phrases:

- **Annotation triggers**: "annotate", "cell type", "label clusters" → `handoff_to_annotation_expert`
- **DE triggers**: "differential expression", "DE analysis", "pseudobulk" → `handoff_to_de_analysis_expert`
- **Pathway triggers**: "pathway analysis", "enrichment", "GO terms" → `handoff_to_de_analysis_expert`

### Standard Workflows

The system prompt defines two canonical analysis sequences. The **SC Standard Workflow** (10 steps): `check_data_status` → `detect_doublets` → `filter_and_normalize` → `select_variable_features` → `run_pca` → `integrate_batches` → `compute_neighbors_and_embed` → `cluster_cells` → `find_marker_genes` → `handoff_to_annotation_expert`. The **Bulk Standard Workflow** (7 steps): `import_bulk_counts` → `merge_sample_metadata` → `assess_bulk_sample_quality` → `filter_bulk_genes` → `normalize_bulk_counts` → `prepare_bulk_for_de` → `handoff_to_de_analysis_expert`. The `cluster_cells` tool can execute steps 4–9 of the SC workflow automatically as a full pipeline, or individual composable tools can be used for fine-grained control.

Sources: [config.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/agents/transcriptomics/config.py#L1-L146), [shared_tools.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/agents/transcriptomics/shared_tools.py#L1-L200), [transcriptomics_expert.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/agents/transcriptomics/transcriptomics_expert.py#L200-L400), [prompts.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/agents/transcriptomics/prompts.py#L1-L200)

## Annotation Expert — Sub-Agent

The **Annotation Expert** is a child agent (`supervisor_accessible=False`) that handles all cell type annotation workflows for single-cell data. It exposes 11 tools covering the full annotation lifecycle:

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `annotate_cell_types_auto` | Automated marker-based annotation using built-in or custom marker dictionaries |
| `score_gene_set` | Score cells against a user-provided gene list |
| `manually_annotate_clusters` | Direct cluster-to-celltype assignment |
| `collapse_clusters_to_celltype` | Merge multiple clusters into one cell type |
| `mark_clusters_as_debris` | Flag clusters as debris for QC exclusion |
| `suggest_debris_clusters` | Smart suggestions for potential debris/doublet clusters |
| `review_annotation_assignments` | Audit current annotation coverage and gaps |
| `apply_annotation_template` | Apply tissue-specific annotation templates (via `AnnotationTemplateService`) |
| `export_annotation_mapping` | Export annotations as JSON for reuse |
| `import_annotation_mapping` | Import and apply saved annotations |
| `annotate_cell_types_semantic` | Semantic annotation via Cell Ontology (requires vector search) |

The agent initializes `ManualAnnotationService`, `AnnotationTemplateService`, and `EnhancedSingleCellService` as stateless services. It also performs a lazy availability check for `VectorSearchService` — if the `lobster-vector` package is installed and the component registry returns a vector search service, the semantic annotation tool gains additional capabilities via Cell Ontology embeddings. The `annotate_cell_types_auto` tool uses a built-in marker database with 10 common cell types (T cells, B cells, NK cells, Monocytes, Dendritic cells, Neutrophils, Platelets, Endothelial, Fibroblasts, Epithelial) and supports custom `reference_markers` overrides. All annotation operations store results as new modalities with `_annotated` suffix and log provenance via `AnalysisStep` IR for [Notebook Export](13-notebook-export-pipeline).

Sources: [annotation_expert.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/agents/transcriptomics/annotation_expert.py#L1-L200), [enhanced_singlecell_service.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/services/analysis/enhanced_singlecell_service.py#L1-L100)

## DE Analysis Expert — Sub-Agent

The **DE Analysis Expert** handles all differential expression workflows for both single-cell (via pseudobulk) and bulk RNA-seq. It is the most scientifically rigorous agent in the transcriptomics package, with critical fixes documented in its module docstring:

1. **Raw counts requirement**: DESeq2 requires raw integer counts from `adata.raw.X`, not normalized `adata.X`. The `_extract_raw_counts()` helper prefers `adata.raw.X` and emits a warning when falling back to `adata.X`.
2. **Minimum replicate threshold**: Changed from 2 to **3** for stable variance estimation in pyDESeq2.
3. **Low-power warning**: Any condition with fewer than 4 replicates triggers an explicit warning about insufficient statistical power.

The DE workflow follows this pipeline: **pseudobulk aggregation** → **formula-based experimental design** → **pyDESeq2 analysis** → **pathway enrichment**. The `DifferentialFormulaService` parses R-style formulas (e.g., `~condition + batch`) into design matrices, supporting complex experimental designs with covariates and reference levels. The `PseudobulkService` aggregates single-cell counts at the sample-celltype level using configurable methods (`sum`, `mean`, `median`) with a minimum cells threshold (default: 10 cells per sample-celltype combination).

| DE Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `run_pseudobulk_de` | Aggregate SC → pseudobulk, then run pyDESeq2 |
| `run_formula_de` | Formula-based DE with covariates |
| `run_deseq2_bulk` | Direct bulk RNA-seq DE via pyDESeq2 |
| `iterate_de_analysis` | Iterative DE with comparison across runs |
| `run_pathway_enrichment` | GO/KEGG pathway analysis (premium feature) |

Pathway enrichment is a **premium feature** — it lazy-imports `PathwayEnrichmentService` and gracefully degrades if the package is unavailable, following Lobster's free/commercial tiering model.

Sources: [de_analysis_expert.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/agents/transcriptomics/de_analysis_expert.py#L1-L200), [pseudobulk_service.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/services/analysis/pseudobulk_service.py#L1-L100), [differential_formula_service.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/services/analysis/differential_formula_service.py#L1-L100)

## Genomics Expert — Parent Orchestrator

The **Genomics Expert** handles whole genome sequencing (VCF) and SNP array (PLINK) data. Unlike the transcriptomics expert which auto-detects data type, the genomics expert requires explicit format selection through its loading tools. It supports two data adapters:

- **VCFAdapter** (`cyvcf2`-based): Loads `.vcf`, `.vcf.gz`, `.bcf` files with optional region filtering, sample subsetting, and PASS variant filtering. Supports a `max_variants` cap (default: 100,000) to manage memory for large cohorts.
- **PLINKAdapter** (`bed-reader`-based): Loads `.bed/.bim/.fam` files with optional MAF pre-filtering.

### QC Thresholds

The genomics agent follows UK Biobank–inspired QC standards, defined in `config.py`:

| Parameter | Default | Conservative | Permissive (Rare Variants) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sample call rate | 0.95 | 0.98 | 0.95 |
| Variant call rate | 0.95 | 0.99 | 0.95 |
| Min MAF | 0.01 | 0.05 | 0.001 |
| HWE p-value | 1e-6 | 1e-6 | 1e-10 |
| LD threshold (r²) | 0.2 | — | — |
| Kinship threshold | 0.125 | — | — |
| Clumping window | 250 kb | — | — |

The critical operational rule is **filter order matters**: always `filter_samples()` first, then `filter_variants()`, because sample quality affects variant metric calculations. After QC, LD pruning must precede PCA and GWAS. If GWAS produces a genomic inflation factor (λGC) > 1.1, the agent must calculate population structure PCs on LD-pruned data and re-run GWAS with PC covariates.

### GWAS Pipeline

The `GWASService` wraps `sgkit` for genome-wide association studies, supporting linear regression (continuous phenotypes) and logistic regression (binary phenotypes). Results include λGC, significant variant counts, and top hits. After clumping, the agent delegates clinical interpretation to `variant_analysis_expert`.

Sources: [genomics_expert.py](packages/lobster-genomics/lobster/agents/genomics/genomics_expert.py#L1-L200), [config.py](packages/lobster-genomics/lobster/agents/genomics/config.py#L1-L37), [gwas_service.py](packages/lobster-genomics/lobster/services/analysis/gwas_service.py#L1-L100)

## Variant Analysis Expert — Sub-Agent

The **Variant Analysis Expert** is a child agent (`supervisor_accessible=False`) handling post-GWAS clinical variant interpretation. Its canonical workflow is a sequential pipeline: `normalize_variants` → `predict_consequences` → `query_population_frequencies` → `query_clinical_databases` → `prioritize_variants`. For single-variant lookups, `lookup_variant()` provides a comprehensive one-shot query by rsID or coordinates.

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `normalize_variants` | Left-align indels, split multiallelic variants |
| `predict_consequences` | VEP batch annotation with SIFT/PolyPhen/CADD |
| `query_population_frequencies` | gnomAD allele frequency lookup |
| `query_clinical_databases` | ClinVar pathogenicity and disease associations |
| `prioritize_variants` | Rank by consequence severity + frequency + pathogenicity |
| `lookup_variant` | Single-variant comprehensive lookup |
| `retrieve_sequence` | Ensembl sequence fetch |

Variant prioritization uses a weighted scoring system: **consequence severity (0–0.4)** + **population rarity (0–0.3)** + **pathogenicity (0–0.3)**, producing a composite score from 0 to 1.0. The agent recommends normalization before annotation for consistent variant representation, and for batch sizes >10K variants, recommends `genebe` over `ensembl_vep` for faster processing.

Sources: [variant_analysis_expert.py](packages/lobster-genomics/lobster/agents/genomics/variant_analysis_expert.py#L1-L200)

## State Management

Each agent defines a typed state class extending LangGraph's `AgentState`, enabling structured state propagation during agent handoffs. The transcriptomics package registers three state classes via entry points:

| State Class | Agent | Key Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `TranscriptomicsExpertState` | Parent | `data_type`, `quality_metrics`, `clustering_parameters`, `marker_genes` |
| `AnnotationExpertState` | Annotation child | `cell_type_annotations`, `annotation_confidence`, `debris_clusters`, `pending_annotations` |
| `DEAnalysisExpertState` | DE child | `experimental_design`, `formula`, `de_results`, `iteration_history`, `pathway_results` |

All state classes include a `next: str` field (for LangGraph routing), `task_description`, and `intermediate_outputs: Dict[str, Any]` for cross-cutting data exchange. The genomics package does not register separate state classes — it relies on the base `AgentState` provided by LangGraph.

Sources: [state.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/agents/transcriptomics/state.py#L1-L101), [pyproject.toml](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/pyproject.toml#L65-L68)

## Service Architecture

Both packages follow a **stateless service pattern** — services are initialized without persistent state and return a consistent 3-tuple: `(AnnData, stats_dict, AnalysisStep)`. This pattern enables provenance tracking via the `AnalysisStep` IR and ensures services are safe for concurrent use.

### Transcriptomics Services

| Service | Location | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `QualityService` | `services/quality/quality_service.py` | QC metrics calculation and assessment |
| `PreprocessingService` | `services/quality/preprocessing_service.py` | Filtering and normalization |
| `ClusteringService` | `services/analysis/` (core package) | Leiden/Louvain clustering, UMAP |
| `EnhancedSingleCellService` | `services/analysis/enhanced_singlecell_service.py` | Doublet detection, annotation, pathway enrichment |
| `BulkRNASeqService` | `services/analysis/` (core package) | Bulk RNA-seq import and processing |
| `BulkPreprocessingService` | `services/analysis/bulk_preprocessing_service.py` | Bulk-specific preprocessing |
| `PseudobulkService` | `services/analysis/pseudobulk_service.py` | SC → pseudobulk aggregation |
| `DifferentialFormulaService` | `services/analysis/differential_formula_service.py` | R-formula parsing and design matrices |
| `ManualAnnotationService` | `services/metadata/manual_annotation_service.py` | Manual annotation state management |
| `AnnotationTemplateService` | `services/templates/annotation_templates.py` | Tissue-specific annotation templates |
| `BulkVisualizationService` | `services/visualization/bulk_visualization_service.py` | Bulk RNA-seq visualizations |

### Genomics Services

| Service | Location | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `GenomicsQualityService` | `services/quality/genomics_quality_service.py` | VCF/PLINK QC metrics |
| `GWASService` | `services/analysis/gwas_service.py` | GWAS via sgkit |
| `VariantAnnotationService` | `services/analysis/variant_annotation_service.py` | VEP, gnomAD, ClinVar queries |

Sources: [pseudobulk_service.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/services/analysis/pseudobulk_service.py#L1-L100), [gwas_service.py](packages/lobster-genomics/lobster/services/analysis/gwas_service.py#L1-L100), [enhanced_singlecell_service.py](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/lobster/services/analysis/enhanced_singlecell_service.py#L1-L100)

## Package Dependencies and Optional Features

Both packages depend on `lobster-ai~=1.1.0` as their core framework. The transcriptomics package has a rich dependency set including `scanpy`, `leidenalg`, `pydeseq2`, and `plotly`, with optional extras for platform-specific or specialized capabilities:

| Optional Extra | Package | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `seurat-v3` | `scikit-misc>=0.5.1` | Seurat v3 HVG flavor (requires Fortran compiler on aarch64) |
| `doublet-detection` | `scrublet>=0.2.3` | Doublet detection for single-cell QC |
| `batch-integration` | `harmonypy>=0.0.6` | Harmony batch correction |

The genomics package has a single optional extra: `genebe>=0.2.0` for faster batch variant annotation. Both packages require Python `>=3.12,<3.14`.

Sources: [pyproject.toml](packages/lobster-transcriptomics/pyproject.toml#L1-L81), [pyproject.toml](packages/lobster-genomics/pyproject.toml#L1-L56)

## Provenance and Notebook Export

Every tool that performs a computational step creates an `AnalysisStep` IR object containing the operation name, library, code template, imports, parameters, and parameter schema. This IR is logged via `data_manager.log_tool_usage()` and can be assembled into reproducible Jupyter notebooks through the [Notebook Export Pipeline](13-notebook-export-pipeline). The `ParameterSpec` entries mark which parameters are `papermill_injectable`, enabling parameterized notebook re-execution. For example, `load_vcf` creates an IR with `file_path` and `modality_name` as injectable parameters, so the exported notebook can be re-run on different VCF files without code modification.

Sources: [genomics_expert.py](packages/lobster-genomics/lobster/agents/genomics/genomics_expert.py#L200-L280)

# Proteomics and Metabolomics Agents



The **Proteomics** and **Metabolomics** domain packages encode omics-specific intelligence as LangGraph ReAct agents, each backed by stateless service classes and platform-aware configuration that auto-detects instrument characteristics from data alone. The proteomics package operates as a **parent-child agent hierarchy** — a parent orchestrator that delegates differential expression, biomarker discovery, and peptide analysis to specialized sub-agents — while the metabolomics package runs as a single flat agent structured for future sub-agent extraction. Both packages share the same architectural DNA: factory functions that wire `DataManagerV2` to service instances, `AgentRegistryConfig` declarations for supervisor discovery, and platform-detection scoring systems that silently select correct defaults so users never need to specify whether their data came from a mass spectrometer or an Olink panel.

Sources: [\_\_init\_\_.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/__init__.py#L1-L13), [\_\_init\_\_.py](packages/lobster-metabolomics/lobster/agents/metabolomics/__init__.py#L1-L5)

## Agent Topology and Hierarchy

The proteomics package deploys a **three-tier delegation model**: the parent `proteomics_expert` handles QC, preprocessing, and pattern analysis directly, then hands off downstream tasks to one of three child agents. The metabolomics package uses a single `metabolomics_expert` with no children in its current version, though its `AGENT_CONFIG` explicitly sets `child_agents=None` with a comment indicating planned extraction. This asymmetry reflects a deliberate design decision — proteomics has more analytically distinct workflows (DE analysis vs. network/survival vs. peptide computation) that benefit from isolated tool sets and prompts, while metabolomics workflows are more sequential and share tighter state dependencies.

```mermaid
graph TD
    SUP[Supervisor Agent] -->|handoff_to_proteomics_expert| PE[Proteomics Expert<br/>Parent Orchestrator]
    SUP -->|handoff_to_metabolomics_expert| ME[Metabolomics Expert<br/>Flat Agent]
    
    PE -->|handoff_to_proteomics_de_analysis_expert| DE[DE Analysis Expert<br/>7 tools]
    PE -->|handoff_to_biomarker_discovery_expert| BD[Biomarker Discovery Expert<br/>7 tools]
    PE -->|handoff_to_peptide_expert| PQ[Peptide Expert<br/>8 tools]
    
    PE -.->|shared_tools: 10+ tools| S1[(QC · Filter · Normalize<br/>Impute · Patterns · Status)]
    ME -.->|shared_tools: 10 tools| S2[(QC · Filter · Impute<br/>Normalize · Stats · Annotate)]
    
    style PE fill:#4A90D9,color:#fff
    style ME fill:#7B68EE,color:#fff
    style DE fill:#5BA55B,color:#fff
    style BD fill:#D4A017,color:#fff
    style PQ fill:#C0392B,color:#fff
```

The delegation protocol is **mandatory** — the proteomics parent agent's prompt contains explicit instructions to immediately invoke handoff tools for DE, time course, correlation, pathway, network, survival, and biomarker tasks rather than attempting them directly. Each child agent is registered with `supervisor_accessible=False`, meaning the supervisor cannot route to them directly; delegation always flows through the parent.

Sources: [proteomics_expert.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/proteomics_expert.py#L18-L36), [metabolomics_expert.py](packages/lobster-metabolomics/lobster/agents/metabolomics/metabolomics_expert.py#L13-L26), [prompts.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/prompts.py#L65-L100)

## Agent Registry Configuration

Every agent exposes an `AGENT_CONFIG` dataclass at module level — placed before heavy imports so the supervisor's entry-point scanner can discover agents without triggering transitive dependency chains. This configuration drives the [Agent Registry and Discovery](7-agent-registry-and-discovery) system and defines handoff tool names, descriptions, and child relationships.

| Field | Proteomics Expert | DE Analysis Expert | Biomarker Discovery Expert | Peptide Expert | Metabolomics Expert |
|-------|------------------|--------------------|---------------------------|----------------|---------------------|
| **name** | `proteomics_expert` | `proteomics_de_analysis_expert` | `biomarker_discovery_expert` | `peptide_expert` | `metabolomics_expert` |
| **supervisor_accessible** | `True` | `False` | `False` | `False` | `True` |
| **child_agents** | 3 children | None | None | None | None |
| **handoff_tool** | `handoff_to_proteomics_expert` | `handoff_to_proteomics_de_analysis_expert` | None (parent-delegated) | `handoff_to_peptide_expert` | `handoff_to_metabolomics_expert` |
| **tier_requirement** | `free` | `free` | `free` | `free` | `free` |

The `supervisor_accessible=False` flag on child agents enforces the delegation boundary — the supervisor's routing table only contains entries for the two parent-accessible agents. The `tier_requirement="free"` across all agents signals that commercial value lives in the Omics-OS Cloud orchestration layer, not in individual agent access.

Sources: [proteomics_expert.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/proteomics_expert.py#L18-L36), [de_analysis_expert.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/de_analysis_expert.py#L22-L34), [biomarker_discovery_expert.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/biomarker_discovery_expert.py#L19-L30), [peptide_expert.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/peptide_expert.py#L15-L25), [metabolomics_expert.py](packages/lobster-metabolomics/lobster/agents/metabolomics/metabolomics_expert.py#L13-L26)

## Platform Auto-Detection

Both packages implement a **scoring-based platform detection system** that examines AnnData metadata columns and data characteristics to identify the instrument platform, then applies platform-specific defaults for QC thresholds, normalization methods, and imputation strategies. This is the central innovation that allows agents to handle heterogeneous data without user configuration.

### Proteomics Platform Detection

The proteomics `detect_platform_type` function scores data against two platform profiles — **mass spectrometry** (DDA/DIA) and **affinity** (Olink, SomaScan, Luminex) — using five signal categories:

| Signal Category | Mass Spec Indicators (+score) | Affinity Indicators (+score) |
|----------------|-------------------------------|------------------------------|
| **var columns** | `n_peptides`, `n_unique_peptides`, `sequence_coverage`, `protein_group` (+2 each) | `antibody_id`, `antibody_clone`, `panel_type`, `npx_value` (+2 each) |
| **contaminant markers** | `is_contaminant`, `is_reverse` columns (+3) | — |
| **plate markers** | — | `plate_id`, `plate_number` in obs (+2) |
| **missing rate** | >30% missing (+3) | <30% missing (implicit) |
| **protein count** | >3000 proteins (+2) | <200 proteins (+2) |

When scores tie or both are zero, the function returns `"unknown"` and callers default to mass spec with a warning.

### Metabolomics Platform Detection

The metabolomics detector scores against three platforms — **LC-MS**, **GC-MS**, and **NMR** — using var column hints, `uns["platform"]` metadata, and missing rate as a tiebreaker:

| Signal | LC-MS (+score) | GC-MS (+score) | NMR (+score) |
|--------|----------------|----------------|--------------|
| **var columns** | `retention_time`, `mz`, `adduct`, `rt`, `precursor_mz` (+2 each) | `ri`, `retention_index`, `kovats_index`, `derivatization` (+3 each) | `ppm`, `chemical_shift`, `bin_start`, `bin_end` (+3 each) |
| **uns platform** | `"lc-ms"`, `"lcms"`, `"liquid"` (+5) | `"gc-ms"`, `"gcms"`, `"gas"` (+5) | `"nmr"`, `"nuclear"`, `"1h"`, `"13c"` (+5) |
| **missing rate** | 20–60% | 10–40% | 0–10% |

> [!TIP]
> Both detection functions accept a `force_type` override parameter, which bypasses scoring entirely and directly validates against `PLATFORM_CONFIGS` keys. Use this when you know the platform but the data lacks discriminating metadata — for example, a processed expression matrix stripped of original m/z or peptide columns.

Sources: [config.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/config.py#L70-L259), [config.py](packages/lobster-metabolomics/lobster/agents/metabolomics/config.py#L63-L241)

## Platform-Specific Defaults

Platform detection feeds directly into `PlatformConfig` / `MetabPlatformConfig` dataclasses that define **every default parameter** an agent needs. These configs are not advisory — tools read them programmatically via `get_qc_defaults()` and `get_normalization_defaults()` to populate method selections, thresholds, and imputation strategies without user input.

### Proteomics Platform Comparison

| Parameter | Mass Spectrometry | Affinity Proteomics |
|-----------|------------------|---------------------|
| **Missing rate range** | 30–70% (MNAR) | 0–30% (MAR) |
| **Max missing/sample** | 70% | 30% |
| **Max missing/protein** | 80% | 50% |
| **CV threshold** | 50% | 30% |
| **Min proteins/sample** | 100 | 20 |
| **Normalization** | median + log2 | quantile (no log) |
| **Imputation** | `keep` (preserve MNAR) | `impute_knn` (MAR imputation) |
| **Fold change cutoff** | 1.5× | 1.2× |
| **PCA components** | 15 | 10 |
| **Platform-specific** | min 2 peptides/protein, remove contaminants | correct plate effects, check antibody specificity |

The most consequential difference is the **missing value strategy**: mass spectrometry data exhibits Missing Not At Random (MNAR) patterns where absent values reflect true biological absence below detection limits, so the default `keep` strategy preserves this information. Affinity data exhibits Missing At Random (MAR) patterns from technical failures, making KNN imputation appropriate.

### Metabolomics Platform Comparison

| Parameter | LC-MS | GC-MS | NMR |
|-----------|-------|-------|-----|
| **Missing rate range** | 20–60% | 10–40% | 0–10% |
| **Max missing/sample** | 60% | 40% | 10% |
| **Max missing/feature** | 80% | 60% | 20% |
| **QC RSD threshold** | 30% | 25% | 20% |
| **Min features/sample** | 50 | 30 | 100 |
| **Normalization** | PQN + log2 | TIC + log2 | PQN (no log) |
| **Imputation** | KNN | min/2 | median |
| **Fold change cutoff** | 1.5× | 2.0× | 1.5× |

> [!TIP]
> The GC-MS fold change threshold of 2.0× (higher than LC-MS or NMR) reflects GC-MS's superior chromatographic reproducibility — features that pass the tighter RSD filter should show larger effect sizes to be considered biologically meaningful.

Sources: [config.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/config.py#L62-L131), [config.py](packages/lobster-metabolomics/lobster/agents/metabolomics/config.py#L55-L143)

## State Schemas and Agent State Design

Each agent declares a state class that extends LangGraph's `AgentState` with domain-specific fields. These states are **not shared across agents** — delegation passes task descriptions, not state objects, which keeps the hierarchy loosely coupled.

### Proteomics State Hierarchy

```
ProteomicsExpertState          ← Parent: QC, platform, normalization, pattern analysis
├── DEAnalysisExpertState      ← Child: comparison groups, DE/time course/correlation results
├── BiomarkerDiscoveryExpertState ← Child: WGCNA modules, survival, biomarker candidates
└── PeptideExpertState         ← Child: properties, activity, digestion, variants
```

All four states inherit `next: str = ""` and `task_description: str = ""` from the `AgentState` base, plus an `intermediate_outputs: Dict[str, Any]` for cross-tool communication within a single agent's execution. The parent state additionally carries `platform_type`, `platform_defaults`, `missing_value_info`, and `normalization_info` — the platform detection results that downstream tools read.

### Metabolomics State

`MetabolomicsExpertState` is a single flat state with fields for `quality_metrics`, `platform_defaults`, `missing_value_info`, `normalization_info`, `statistical_results`, `multivariate_results`, and `annotation_results` — reflecting the sequential pipeline nature of untargeted metabolomics where each stage's output feeds the next.

Sources: [state.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/state.py#L1-L126), [state.py](packages/lobster-metabolomics/lobster/agents/metabolomics/state.py#L1-L50)

## Tool Inventories by Agent

Each agent's tools are constructed through factory functions that close over the `DataManagerV2` and service instances, producing LangChain `@tool`-decorated functions with AQUADIF category metadata and provenance tracking.

### Proteomics Expert (Parent) — Shared Tools + Inline Tools

The parent agent receives tools from two sources: `create_shared_tools()` produces the core QC/preprocessing/analysis tools, and a small number of platform-specific tools are defined inline in the factory function.

| # | Tool | Category | Source | Provenance |
|---|------|----------|--------|------------|
| 1 | `import_proteomics_data` | IMPORT | shared_tools | Yes |
| 2 | `import_affinity_data` | IMPORT | shared_tools | Yes |
| 3 | `import_ptm_sites` | IMPORT | shared_tools | Yes |
| 4 | `check_proteomics_status` | UTILITY | shared_tools | No |
| 5 | `assess_proteomics_quality` | QUALITY | shared_tools | Yes |
| 6 | `filter_proteomics_data` | PREPROCESS | shared_tools | Yes |
| 7 | `normalize_proteomics_data` | PREPROCESS | shared_tools | Yes |
| 8 | `handle_missing_values` | PREPROCESS | shared_tools | Yes |
| 9 | `correct_batch_effects` | PREPROCESS | shared_tools | Yes |
| 10 | `analyze_proteomics_patterns` | ANALYZE | shared_tools | Yes |
| 11 | `select_variable_proteins` | ANALYZE | shared_tools | Yes |
| 12 | `create_proteomics_summary` | UTILITY | shared_tools | Yes |
| 13 | `add_peptide_mapping` | UTILITY | inline (deprecated) | No |
| 14 | `validate_antibody_specificity` | QUALITY | inline | Yes |

The deprecated `add_peptide_mapping` tool now returns a warning message directing users to `import_proteomics_data`, which automatically extracts peptide counts, unique peptides, and sequence coverage from MaxQuant/DIA-NN/Spectronaut parser output.

### DE Analysis Expert — 7 Tools

| # | Tool | Purpose |
|---|------|---------|
| 1 | `find_differential_proteins` | Statistical testing with platform-aware method selection and FDR |
| 2 | `run_time_course_analysis` | Longitudinal proteomics with repeated measures |
| 3 | `run_correlation_analysis` | Protein-trait continuous variable correlation |
| 4 | `run_pathway_enrichment` | GO/Reactome/KEGG via core PathwayEnrichmentService |
| 5 | `run_differential_ptm_analysis` | Phospho/PTM site-level differential analysis |
| 6 | `run_kinase_enrichment` | KSEA kinase substrate enrichment analysis |
| 7 | `run_string_network_analysis` | STRING protein-protein interaction networks |

The DE expert performs a minimum sample size check — if the smallest group has fewer than 3 samples, it returns an error message with group sizes rather than attempting unreliable statistical testing.

### Biomarker Discovery Expert — 7 Tools

| # | Tool | Purpose |
|---|------|---------|
| 1 | `identify_coexpression_modules` | WGCNA-lite module identification with color labels |
| 2 | `correlate_modules_with_traits` | Module-trait eigengene correlation |
| 3 | `perform_survival_analysis` | Cox proportional hazards regression |
| 4 | `find_survival_biomarkers` | Batch Kaplan-Meier biomarker screening |
| 5 | `select_biomarker_panel` | Multi-method feature selection (LASSO, stability, Boruta) |
| 6 | `evaluate_biomarker_panel` | Nested cross-validation with AUC reporting |
| 7 | `extract_hub_proteins` | Hub protein extraction via kME from WGCNA modules |

### Peptide Expert — 8 Domain Tools

| # | Tool | Purpose |
|---|------|---------|
| 1 | `import_peptide_sequences` | Load from FASTA/CSV/TSV with validation against standard amino acids |
| 2 | `calculate_peptide_properties` | MW, pI, charge, GRAVY, Boman index, etc. |
| 3 | `predict_peptide_activity` | Heuristic scoring for antimicrobial/CPP/toxicity |
| 4 | `simulate_enzymatic_digestion` | In silico tryptic/chymotryptic/pepsin/Lys-C/Asp-N/Glu-C digest |
| 5 | `filter_peptides` | Threshold filtering on length, charge, hydrophobicity, activity |
| 6 | `generate_variants` | — |
| 7 | `annotate_bioactive_peptides` | — |
| 8 | `export_peptide_library` | — |

### Metabolomics Expert — 10 Tools

| # | Tool | Category | Purpose |
|---|------|----------|---------|
| 1 | `assess_metabolomics_quality` | QUALITY | RSD, TIC distribution, QC reproducibility, missing profiling |
| 2 | `filter_metabolomics_features` | PREPROCESS | Prevalence, RSD, and blank ratio filtering |
| 3 | `handle_missing_values` | PREPROCESS | KNN/min/LOD-half/median/MICE imputation |
| 4 | `normalize_metabolomics` | PREPROCESS | PQN/TIC/IS/median/quantile + optional log2 |
| 5 | `correct_batch_effects` | PREPROCESS | ComBat/QC-RLSC/median centering |
| 6 | `run_metabolomics_statistics` | ANALYZE | Univariate tests with FDR + fold change |
| 7 | `run_multivariate_analysis` | ANALYZE | PCA, PLS-DA (VIP scores), OPLS-DA |
| 8 | `annotate_metabolites` | ANNOTATE | m/z matching against ~80-metabolite reference database |
| 9 | `analyze_lipid_classes` | ANNOTATE | Annotation-based or m/z range-based lipid classification |
| 10 | `run_pathway_enrichment` | ANALYZE | KEGG/Reactome/GO via core PathwayEnrichmentService |

Sources: [shared_tools.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/shared_tools.py#L1-L2794), [de_analysis_expert.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/de_analysis_expert.py#L86-L1530), [biomarker_discovery_expert.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/biomarker_discovery_expert.py#L72-L1562), [peptide_tools.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/peptide_tools.py#L1-L746), [shared_tools.py](packages/lobster-metabolomics/lobster/agents/metabolomics/shared_tools.py#L1-L1063)

## Standard Workflows

The agent prompts encode **prescribed analysis pipelines** as numbered step sequences. These workflows represent the recommended analysis order for each platform type, ensuring that filtering precedes imputation, normalization follows imputation, and statistical tests operate on properly preprocessed data.

### Proteomics Workflows

**MS Discovery Proteomics** — the most common workflow — imports data through the dedicated parser, runs QC with mass-spec metrics, filters contaminants and low-peptide proteins, applies median + log2 normalization, then delegates to the DE sub-agent for differential analysis and downstream interpretation:

```
1. import_proteomics_data("path/to/proteinGroups.txt")  → Auto-detect MaxQuant/DIA-NN/Spectronaut
2. check_proteomics_status()                              → Verify import & platform detection
3. assess_proteomics_quality("modality")                  → QC with MS-specific metrics
4. filter_proteomics_data("modality_assessed")            → Remove contaminants, low-peptide proteins
5. normalize_proteomics_data("modality_filtered")         → Median + log2
6. correct_batch_effects("modality_normalized")           → If multi-batch (OPTIONAL)
7. select_variable_proteins("modality_normalized")        → Optional: top variable proteins
8. analyze_proteomics_patterns("modality_normalized")     → PCA/clustering
9. → handoff_to_proteomics_de_analysis_expert             → DE analysis + pathway/network
10. create_proteomics_summary()                           → Final report
```

**Affinity Proteomics** (Olink/SomaScan/Luminex) follows a similar structure but adds platform-specific steps: LOD quality assessment, bridge sample normalization for multi-plate studies, plate effect correction, and antibody specificity validation:

```
1. import_affinity_data("path/to/data.npx")              → Auto-detect Olink/SomaScan/Luminex
2. check_proteomics_status()                              → Verify import & platform detection
3. assess_proteomics_quality("modality")                  → QC with LOD metrics
4. assess_lod_quality("modality")                         → Detailed per-protein below-LOD %
5. filter_proteomics_data("modality_assessed")            → Remove failed antibodies
6. normalize_bridge_samples("modality_filtered")          → If multi-plate Olink
7. correct_plate_effects("modality_normalized")           → Residual plate effects
8. normalize_proteomics_data("modality_corrected")        → Quantile + impute
9. validate_antibody_specificity("modality_normalized")   → Cross-reactivity check
10. analyze_proteomics_patterns("modality_validated")     → PCA/clustering
11. → handoff_to_proteomics_de_analysis_expert            → DE analysis
12. → handoff_to_biomarker_discovery_expert               → Optional: network/survival/panel
```

**PTM/Phosphoproteomics** is a specialized workflow requiring paired import of both protein-level and PTM-level data, with separate PTM-to-protein normalization that isolates phosphorylation changes from protein abundance changes before differential analysis.

### Metabolomics Workflows

**Untargeted LC-MS** — the default metabolomics pipeline — chains QC through annotation with 10 sequential steps:

```
1. assess_metabolomics_quality(modality)                  → TIC, RSD, QC samples, missing values
2. filter_metabolomics_features(modality_assessed)        → Prevalence > 0.5, optionally by blank ratio
3. handle_missing_values(modality_filtered, "knn")        → KNN imputation (LC-MS default)
4. normalize_metabolomics(modality_imputed, "pqn", log_transform=True)  → PQN + log2
5. correct_batch_effects(modality_normalized, batch_key)  → If multi-batch
6. run_metabolomics_statistics(modality_normalized, group_column)  → Univariate + fold changes
7. run_multivariate_analysis(modality_normalized, "pca")  → Unsupervised overview
8. run_multivariate_analysis(modality_normalized, "plsda", group_column=...)  → Supervised
9. annotate_metabolites(modality_normalized, ppm_tolerance=10, ion_mode="positive")  → Putative IDs
10. run_pathway_enrichment(modality_statistics, database="KEGG_2021_Human")  → Biological interpretation
```

GC-MS and NMR workflows follow the same sequence with parameter substitutions: GC-MS uses TIC normalization + min/2 imputation, while NMR uses PQN without log transform + median imputation.

Sources: [prompts.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/prompts.py#L102-L200), [prompts.py](packages/lobster-metabolomics/lobster/agents/metabolomics/prompts.py#L86-L200)

## Service Architecture

All computational work is delegated to **stateless service classes** instantiated inside the agent factory functions. This separation means agents contain zero business logic — they are thin orchestration layers that validate inputs, call service methods, store results via `DataManagerV2`, and format responses. Every service method returns a three-tuple of `(adata_result, stats_dict, analysis_ir)` enabling both data lineage tracking and human-readable reporting.

### Proteomics Service Map

| Service | Location | Used By |
|---------|----------|---------|
| `ProteomicsQualityService` | `services/quality/` | Parent (shared_tools) |
| `ProteomicsPreprocessingService` | `services/quality/` | Parent (shared_tools) |
| `ProteomicsAnalysisService` | `services/analysis/` | Parent (shared_tools) |
| `ProteomicsDifferentialService` | `services/analysis/` | DE Analysis Expert |
| `ProteomicsPathwayService` | `services/analysis/` | DE Analysis Expert (lazy import) |
| `ProteomicsKinaseService` | `services/analysis/` | DE Analysis Expert (lazy import) |
| `ProteomicsStringService` | `services/analysis/` | DE Analysis Expert (lazy import) |
| `WGCNALiteService` | `services/analysis/` | Biomarker Discovery Expert |
| `ProteomicsSurvivalService` | `services/analysis/` | Biomarker Discovery Expert |
| `ProteomicsVisualizationService` | `services/visualization/` | (available) |
| `PeptidePropertyService` | `services/peptidomics/` | Peptide Expert |
| `PeptideActivityService` | `services/peptidomics/` | Peptide Expert |
| `PeptideDigestionService` | `services/peptidomics/` | Peptide Expert |

### Metabolomics Service Map

| Service | Location | Used By |
|---------|----------|---------|
| `MetabolomicsQualityService` | `services/quality/` | Metabolomics Expert (shared_tools) |
| `MetabolomicsPreprocessingService` | `services/quality/` | Metabolomics Expert (shared_tools) |
| `MetabolomicsAnalysisService` | `services/analysis/` | Metabolomics Expert (shared_tools) |
| `MetabolomicsAnnotationService` | `services/annotation/` | Metabolomics Expert (shared_tools) |

The DE Analysis Expert uses **lazy imports** for downstream services (`ProteomicsPathwayService`, `ProteomicsKinaseService`, `ProteomicsStringService`) — imported inside the factory function rather than at module level — to avoid circular dependencies and reduce cold-start cost for cases where only core DE testing is needed.

Sources: [proteomics_expert.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/proteomics_expert.py#L95-L110), [de_analysis_expert.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/de_analysis_expert.py#L95-L109), [metabolomics_expert.py](packages/lobster-metabolomics/lobster/agents/metabolomics/metabolomics_expert.py#L82-L96)

## Provenance and the Analysis IR

Every tool call that modifies data generates an `AnalysisStep` record — a structured intermediate representation that captures the operation name, parameters, code template, and library dependencies. The `DataManagerV2.log_tool_usage()` method stores these IR records, enabling the [Notebook Export Pipeline](13-notebook-export-pipeline) to reconstruct a reproducible analysis script from the provenance chain.

The `ParameterSpec` schema within each `AnalysisStep` distinguishes between `papermill_injectable` parameters (safe for automated notebook parameterization) and non-injectable ones (like orientation flags that affect code structure). For example, the `file_path` parameter in `import_proteomics_data` is injectable (`papermill_injectable=True`), while `orientation` is not because it determines whether the code template includes a transpose operation.

Sources: [shared_tools.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/shared_tools.py#L117-L176), [biomarker_discovery_expert.py](packages/lobster-proteomics/lobster/agents/proteomics/biomarker_discovery_expert.py#L133-L152)

# Research, ML, and Visualization Agents



The **Research**, **Machine Learning**, and **Visualization** agent packages form the analytical backbone of Lobster's multi-agent pipeline — spanning literature discovery through ML-ready data preparation to publication-quality rendering. Each package is independently installable, registry-discoverable, and connected through the supervisor-mediated orchestration graph. Together they close the loop from "what's known in the literature" to "what the data looks like in a figure," a trajectory that mirrors the actual workflow of a working computational biologist.

Sources: [research_agent.py](/packages/lobster-research/lobster/agents/research/research_agent.py#L1-L55), [machine_learning_expert.py](/packages/lobster-ml/lobster/agents/machine_learning/machine_learning_expert.py#L1-L50), [visualization_expert.py](/packages/lobster-visualization/lobster/agents/visualization_expert.py#L1-L50), [protein_structure_visualization_expert.py](/packages/lobster-structural-viz/lobster/agents/protein_structure_visualization_expert.py#L1-L50)

## Architectural Overview

All four agent packages share a uniform architectural skeleton: an `AgentRegistryConfig` declaration at module top, lazy-loaded services inside the factory function, LangChain `@tool`-decorated functions closing over a shared `DataManagerV2` instance, and a final `create_react_agent` call that wires everything into a LangGraph node. This consistency is not accidental — it is enforced by the scaffold system described in [Scaffold and Package Validation](10-scaffold-and-package-validation).

```mermaid
graph TD
    SUP[Supervisor Agent] -->|handoff_to_research_agent| RA[Research Agent]
    SUP -->|handoff_to_machine_learning_expert| ML[ML Expert]
    SUP -->|handoff_to_visualization_expert_agent| VE[Visualization Expert]
    SUP -->|handoff_to_protein_structure_visualization_expert_agent| SV[Structural Viz Expert]

    ML -->|handoff_to_feature_selection_expert| FS[Feature Selection Expert]
    ML -->|handoff_to_survival_analysis_expert| SA[Survival Analysis Expert]

    RA -->|handoff_to_metadata_assistant| MA[Metadata Assistant]

    RA -.->|DataManagerV2| DM[(DataManagerV2)]
    ML -.->|DataManagerV2| DM
    VE -.->|DataManagerV2| DM
    SV -.->|DataManagerV2| DM

    subgraph "lobster-research"
        RA
    end
    subgraph "lobster-ml"
        ML
        FS
        SA
    end
    subgraph "lobster-visualization"
        VE
    end
    subgraph "lobster-structural-viz"
        SV
    end
```

The supervisor never calls sub-agents of the ML Expert directly — `feature_selection_expert` and `survival_analysis_expert` are declared with `supervisor_accessible=False`, so they can only be reached through their parent. Conversely, the Research Agent can hand off to `metadata_assistant` (a premium-tier feature gated by subscription level). The Visualization and Structural Viz experts have no child agents; they operate as leaf nodes.

Sources: [config.py](/packages/lobster-ml/lobster/agents/machine_learning/config.py#L1-L51), [research_agent.py](/packages/lobster-research/lobster/agents/research/research_agent.py#L14-L28), [visualization_expert.py](/packages/lobster-visualization/lobster/agents/visualization_expert.py#L14-L20), [protein_structure_visualization_expert.py](/packages/lobster-structural-viz/lobster/agents/protein_structure_visualization_expert.py#L14-L20)

## Agent Comparison at a Glance

| Dimension | Research Agent | ML Expert | Visualization Expert | Structural Viz Expert |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Package** | `lobster-research` | `lobster-ml` | `lobster-visualization` | `lobster-structural-viz` |
| **Registry Name** | `research_agent` | `machine_learning_expert` | `visualization_expert_agent` | `protein_structure_visualization_expert_agent` |
| **Tier** | Free (child: premium) | Free | Free | Free |
| **Child Agents** | `metadata_assistant` | `feature_selection_expert`, `survival_analysis_expert` | None | None |
| **Supervisor Accessible** | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Primary Data Flow** | Literature → Dataset metadata → Queue | Modality → Features → Splits → Export | Modality → Plot figures → Workspace | PDB ID → Structure file → 3D render |
| **State Schema** | `ResearchAgentState` | `MachineLearningExpertState` | `VisualizationExpertState` | `ProteinStructureVisualizationExpertState` |
| **Key Services** | ContentAccess, QueuePreparation, MetadataValidation | MLPreparation, FeatureSelection, SurvivalAnalysis | SingleCellVisualization | PyMOLVisualization, StructureAnalysis, ProteinStructureFetch |

Sources: [config.py](/packages/lobster-ml/lobster/agents/machine_learning/config.py#L25-L51), [state.py](/packages/lobster-research/lobster/agents/research/state.py#L1-L61), [visualization_state.py](/packages/lobster-visualization/lobster/agents/visualization_state.py#L1-L40), [structural_viz_state.py](/packages/lobster-structural-viz/lobster/agents/structural_viz_state.py#L1-L44)

## Research Agent

The Research Agent is a **literature-to-metadata orchestrator** that never communicates with end users — it responds only to the supervisor. Its mandate is precise: discover and triage publications and datasets, manage the publication queue, validate metadata, and cache reusable artifacts to the workspace. It explicitly does **not** download data (that is the data expert's job) or run omics analysis.

### Registration and Factory

The agent declares itself at module top via `AgentRegistryConfig`, which the [Agent Registry and Discovery](7-agent-registry-and-discovery) system reads at startup:

```python
AGENT_CONFIG = AgentRegistryConfig(
    name="research_agent",
    display_name="Research Agent",
    description="Handles literature discovery, dataset identification, PDF extraction with AUTOMATIC PMID/DOI resolution...",
    factory_function="lobster.agents.research.research_agent.research_agent",
    handoff_tool_name="handoff_to_research_agent",
    child_agents=["metadata_assistant"],
)
```

The `factory_function` string is the entry point the supervisor calls to instantiate the agent at runtime, passing the shared `DataManagerV2`, callback handlers, delegation tools, and subscription tier.

Sources: [research_agent.py](/packages/lobster-research/lobster/agents/research/research_agent.py#L14-L28)

### Lazy Service Loading

The Research Agent employs **lazy initialization** for its five heaviest services, shaving ~1.2 seconds off import time. Services are loaded only when first invoked by a tool:

| Service | Import Cost | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `ContentAccessService` | 500–800 ms | Full-text publication content retrieval |
| `DataExpertAssistant` | 200–400 ms | Dataset expertise queries |
| `MetadataValidationService` | 200–400 ms | Structured metadata validation with severity levels |
| `QueuePreparationService` | — | Download queue entry creation |
| `UniProtService` / `EnsemblService` | — | Knowledgebase identifier lookups |

Each loader follows the same memoization pattern — a `nonlocal` variable, a `None` check, and a debug log on first load. This is a deliberate architectural choice to keep cold-start latency low when the supervisor routes a request to this agent.

Sources: [research_agent.py](/packages/lobster-research/lobster/agents/research/research_agent.py#L100-L175)

### Operating Principles and Prompt Design

The Research Agent's system prompt encodes five operating principles that govern every tool call it makes: **(1) Data type routing** — match assay to repository using the dynamic `OmicsTypeRegistry` so that transcriptomics queries go to GEO/SRA, proteomics to PRIDE/MassIVE, and so on; **(2) Query discipline** — define technology, organism, disease, and required metadata before searching, using controlled vocabulary; **(3) Metadata-first** — immediately check whether candidate datasets expose required annotations, discarding low-value datasets early; **(4) Cache first** — prefer workspace-cached metadata over re-querying providers; **(5) Stopping rules** — cap discovery at ~10 tool calls per workflow, stopping once 1–3 strong datasets match all criteria.

The routing table is built dynamically from `OMICS_TYPE_REGISTRY`, meaning new omics types added to the registry automatically appear in the agent's prompt without manual updates.

Sources: [prompts.py](/packages/lobster-research/lobster/agents/research/prompts.py#L1-L148)

### State Schema

`ResearchAgentState` extends LangGraph's `AgentState` with research-specific fields organized into five semantic groups:

| Group | Key Fields | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Literature Discovery** | `search_history`, `publications_found`, `literature_cache` | Track searches and cached abstracts/methods |
| **Dataset Discovery** | `datasets_discovered`, `dataset_validation_results`, `related_entries` | Map accessions to metadata and validation outcomes |
| **Queue Management** | `download_queue_entries`, `publication_queue_entries`, `queue_status_tracking` | Track entries through the download pipeline |
| **Content Extraction** | `methods_extracted`, `metadata_extracted`, `identifiers_found` | Store extracted methods, metadata, and cross-references |
| **Workspace** | `cached_content`, `workspace_locations` | Map content identifiers to workspace file paths |

Sources: [state.py](/packages/lobster-research/lobster/agents/research/state.py#L1-L61)

### Metadata Verbosity Control

The config module defines three field sets — `ESSENTIAL_FIELDS`, `STANDARD_FIELDS`, and `VERBOSE_FIELDS` — that the `get_dataset_metadata` tool uses to prevent context overflow when returning GEO metadata. Essential fields (database, accession, title, status, pubmed_id, summary) are always included; standard and verbose fields are added only when the user explicitly requests them. This tiered approach prevents a single metadata query from consuming the LLM's context window.

Sources: [config.py](/packages/lobster-research/lobster/agents/research/config.py#L1-L59)

### Tier-Restricted Delegation

The Research Agent's handoff to `metadata_assistant` is gated by subscription tier. At the free tier, the `get_restricted_handoffs` function identifies `metadata_assistant` as restricted, and the factory function filters the delegation tools list before passing it to `create_react_agent`. If the tool is missing due to tier restrictions, the agent informs the supervisor that a premium upgrade is required — it never silently fails.

Sources: [research_agent.py](/packages/lobster-research/lobster/agents/research/research_agent.py#L56-L97)

## Machine Learning Expert Agent

The ML Expert is a **parent orchestrator** that prepares biological data for model training. It handles ML readiness assessment, feature engineering, data splitting, framework export, and scVI embedding training directly, while **immediately delegating** biomarker discovery to the Feature Selection Expert and time-to-event analysis to the Survival Analysis Expert. The delegation protocol is strict: the agent must *invoke* the handoff tool immediately upon detecting trigger phrases, never merely suggest or recommend delegation.

### Agent Hierarchy

```mermaid
graph TD
    SUP[Supervisor] -->|handoff| ML[Machine Learning Expert]
    ML -->|handoff_to_feature_selection_expert| FS[Feature Selection Expert]
    ML -->|handoff_to_survival_analysis_expert| SA[Survival Analysis Expert]

    ML ---|supervisor_accessible: true| ACC1[Directly reachable by Supervisor]
    FS ---|supervisor_accessible: false| ACC2[Only via ML Expert]
    SA ---|supervisor_accessible: false| ACC3[Only via ML Expert]
```

All three agents are tier-free — the commercial value lives in Omics-OS Cloud, not in agent access restrictions.

Sources: [config.py](/packages/lobster-ml/lobster/agents/machine_learning/config.py#L1-L51)

### Direct Tools

The ML Expert's seven direct tools form a linear preparation pipeline:

| Tool | AQUADIF Category | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `check_ml_ready_modalities` | UTILITY | Assess which modalities have labels, normalization, sufficient sample count |
| `prepare_ml_features` | PREPROCESS | Feature selection (highly_variable, pca, all, marker_genes), scaling, zero handling |
| `create_ml_splits` | PREPROCESS | Stratified train/test/validation splits with class balance |
| `export_for_ml_framework` | PREPROCESS | Export to PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, or NumPy formats |
| `create_ml_analysis_summary` | UTILITY | Comprehensive report of all ML preprocessing steps |
| `check_scvi_availability` | UTILITY | Verify scVI-tools installation |
| `train_scvi_embedding` | ANALYZE | Train scVI deep learning embedding for single-cell data |

> [!TIP]
> The `prepare_ml_features` tool creates a new modality named `{modality_name}_ml_features` in the DataManager rather than mutating the original, preserving the provenance chain for [Provenance Tracking and IR](12-provenance-tracking-and-ir).

The readiness check is particularly informative — it inspects each modality for label columns (`condition`, `cell_type`, `treatment`, `group`, `label`, `class`), normalization status, batch information, and sparsity. For small samples (<50), it warns about regularization needs; for large datasets (>10,000), it notes suitability for deep learning.

Sources: [machine_learning_expert.py](/packages/lobster-ml/lobster/agents/machine_learning/machine_learning_expert.py#L60-L200), [prompts.py](/packages/lobster-ml/lobster/agents/machine_learning/prompts.py#L1-L200)

### Mandatory Delegation Protocol

The ML Expert's prompt enforces an **immediate-action delegation protocol**: when trigger phrases like "feature selection", "biomarker", "survival analysis", or "Cox model" are detected, the agent must invoke the corresponding handoff tool *without asking permission, suggesting, or reporting "delegation needed."* This eliminates the common failure mode where an LLM acknowledges a need but fails to act on it. The decision tree is unambiguous:

